questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Marketing communication can be most comprehensively defined as:

options.a: A one-way process by which a firm announces its prices to buyers
options.b: The physical movement of goods from producers to final consumers
options.c: The set of activities used to design and manufacture new products
options.d: A strategic process of creating, delivering and exchanging value-laden messages to shape customer perceptions and behaviours

questions.explanation: Marketing communication is about the messages a firm creates and shares with its audiences so that they understand it, think well of it and act, for example by buying. Option A is too narrow because it is one-way and only about price, while B describes distribution and C describes product development, which are other parts of marketing.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which invention marked the birth of print advertising by revolutionising the way information was shared?

options.a: The radio, which began carrying commercials in the 1920s
options.b: The printing press, invented by Johannes Gutenberg in the 15th century
options.c: Television, which became the dominant platform by the 1950s
options.d: The Internet, which arrived in the late 20th century

questions.explanation: Before Gutenberg's printing press, information lived in handwritten manuscripts that only the elite could access; printing made mass print advertising possible, and printed adverts soon appeared in 17th-century newspapers. Options A, C and D were important later stages in the history of marketing communication, but they came centuries after print advertising began.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Hotmail's 1996 strategy of adding the line "Get your free email at Hotmail" to every email its users sent is an early example of:

options.a: Personal selling, where a salesperson meets each prospect face-to-face
options.b: Sales promotion, where buyers receive coupons and rebates
options.c: Viral digital marketing, where users spread the message as they use the product
options.d: Publicity, where a news editor writes a story about the firm

questions.explanation: Every email a user sent carried the advert to new people, so the message spread itself from person to person, which is what makes it viral; it helped Hotmail gain millions of users within months. Option A needs face-to-face contact, B relies on incentives such as coupons, and D depends on coverage in the editorial section of the news media, none of which happened here.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: How does marketing communication facilitate the exchange process in a competitive market?

options.a: By physically delivering the product to the buyer's location
options.b: By generating awareness, fostering trust and driving purchase intent among target audiences
options.c: By removing the buyer's freedom to accept or reject the offer
options.d: By removing the need for the two parties to trust each other

questions.explanation: An exchange can only happen when each party knows what the other offers and trusts it enough to take the deal seriously, and marketing communication creates that awareness and trust. Option A describes distribution, not communication. Options C and D are wrong because freedom to accept or reject and mutual trust are conditions that an exchange needs.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the conditions for an exchange to take place?

options.a: There must be at least two parties
options.b: Each party must have something that might be of value to the other
options.c: Each party must be legally bound to accept whatever is offered
options.d: Each party must be able to communicate and deliver what it is offering

questions.explanation: For an exchange to take place, each party must be free to accept or reject what is on offer, so being forced to accept is the opposite of a real condition. Options A, B and D are genuine conditions, along with the requirement that each party trusts the other enough to take the exchange seriously.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which of the following best exemplifies a core component of marketing communication?

options.a: Product prototyping and design iteration
options.b: Setting production quotas for the factory
options.c: Integrated advertising campaigns across multiple channels
options.d: Warehousing and inventory control

questions.explanation: Advertising is one of the main tools of marketing communication, and running it across several channels with one consistent message is what integrated marketing communication means. Option A belongs to product development, while B and D are production and logistics activities rather than ways of communicating with customers.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The primary function of marketing communication in a business is to:

options.a: Determine the production cost of each product
options.b: Set the prices charged to wholesalers and retailers
options.c: Inform, persuade and remind customers so as to sustain their engagement with the brand
options.d: Manage the recruitment and payment of factory workers

questions.explanation: Marketing communication exists to tell customers about a firm and its offers, persuade them to buy and remind them so the brand stays in their minds. Option A is a cost accounting task, B is a pricing decision and D is a human resources task, so none of them is the main job of marketing communication.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A strategic objective of marketing communication is to:

options.a: Reduce the number of products in the firm's range
options.b: Lower the cost of the firm's raw materials
options.c: Influence consumer purchasing patterns through targeted messaging
options.d: Decide where the firm's factories should be located

questions.explanation: Marketing communication objectives such as raising awareness, changing attitudes and influencing purchase intent all aim to shape what consumers buy. Option A is a product range decision, B is a purchasing and cost matter, and D is a production location decision.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A campaign that aims to get customers who currently buy competing products to start buying your brand is pursuing which marketing communication objective?

options.a: Driving brand switching
options.b: Increasing brand awareness
options.c: Changing attitudes
options.d: Conducting research for the company

questions.explanation: Brand switching means moving customers away from a rival brand to yours, which is exactly what this campaign is trying to achieve. Option B is about making people know the business exists, C is about correcting mistaken beliefs about a brand, and D is about reading market trends, so none of them describes winning over a competitor's buyers.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which combination of elements is most representative of marketing communication?

options.a: Advertising, sales promotion and direct marketing
options.b: Product, price and place
options.c: Production, warehousing and transport
options.d: Segmentation, targeting and positioning

questions.explanation: Advertising, sales promotion and direct marketing are all tools of the marketing communication (promotion) mix, used to send messages to target audiences. Option B lists the other elements of the marketing mix apart from promotion, C lists operations and logistics activities, and D describes how a market is divided and targeted, not how a firm communicates.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: In the context of marketing communications, the exchange process is best characterised as:

options.a: A one-way transfer of goods from the seller to the buyer
options.b: A reciprocal creation of value that benefits both the organisation and its customers
options.c: A transaction in which only the seller gains value
options.d: A process in which the buyer cannot reject the offer

questions.explanation: Exchange means obtaining something you want from someone by offering something of value in return, so both sides gain. Options A and C leave out the value flowing back to the other party, and D is wrong because each party must be free to accept or reject the offer.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Marketing communication strategically benefits businesses by:

options.a: Guaranteeing that competitors leave the market
options.b: Removing the need for any market research
options.c: Directly lowering the firm's production costs
options.d: Enhancing brand equity, fostering loyalty and driving repeat purchases

questions.explanation: Good marketing communication builds the brand's value, keeps customers attached to it and encourages them to buy again. Option A overstates what communication can do, B is wrong because communication actually depends on understanding the market, and C is a production matter rather than a communication benefit.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The rise of social media platforms such as MySpace, Facebook and Twitter in the early 2000s changed marketing mainly by:

options.a: Turning it into a two-way conversation in which brands engage directly with customers
options.b: Ending the use of print and broadcast advertising
options.c: Making marketing a one-way broadcast from the firm to its audience
options.d: Removing the need for brands to listen to customers

questions.explanation: Social media lets customers reply, comment and share, so brands now talk with their audiences instead of only talking to them. Option B is false because print and broadcast media are still used, while C and D describe the opposite of the two-way engagement that social media created.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is a role of marketing communications?

options.a: Determining the product's physical features
options.b: Choosing the locations of the firm's warehouses
options.c: Calculating the cost of producing each unit
options.d: Shortening the sales cycle

questions.explanation: By understanding customers' needs, motivations and buying processes and using that insight when engaging them, marketing communications helps customers move to a purchase more quickly. Option A is a product design decision, B is a distribution decision and C is a costing task, so none of them is a communication role.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Making sure that the things that make a firm's products unique are shared with the public, so as to strengthen its competitive advantage, describes which role of marketing communications?

options.a: Maintaining customer loyalty
options.b: Shortening the sales cycle
options.c: Highlighting a competitive edge
options.d: Building brand awareness

questions.explanation: In a crowded marketplace, a firm must tell people about its points of differentiation, and doing this is the role called highlighting a competitive edge. Option A is about keeping a positive bond with existing customers, B is about speeding customers to purchase, and D is about making sure people know the business exists, which is broader than showing what makes it different.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The ultimate aim of marketing communication is to influence:

options.a: Consumer decision-making and buying behaviour
options.b: The firm's factory production schedules
options.c: The firm's choice of raw material suppliers
options.d: The government's tax policy

questions.explanation: Marketing communication is aimed at audiences outside the firm, mainly consumers, to shape how they think, decide and buy. Options B and C are internal operational decisions, and D is set by government rather than being the target of a firm's marketing messages.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The channels and tools that companies use to communicate the necessary message to a target group are collectively called:

options.a: Market segmentation
options.b: Distribution management
options.c: Product development
options.d: Marketing communications (MarCom)

questions.explanation: Marketing communications, shortened to MarCom, are the channels and tools a company uses to get its message to its target group. Option A is about grouping similar consumers, option B is about moving goods to buyers and option C is about creating the offering itself, so none of them is the communicating activity.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is one of the common definitions of marketing communication?

options.a: The internal record-keeping of a firm's sales transactions
options.b: The setting of prices for goods based on production cost
options.c: A continuous interaction between the buyers and sellers in a marketplace
options.d: A one-time announcement made only when a new product is launched

questions.explanation: One common definition sees marketing communication as a continuous interaction between buyers and sellers in a marketplace. Option D is wrong because MarCom is ongoing, not a one-off launch event, while options A and B describe accounting and pricing tasks.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: One definition describes marketing communication as the means companies adopt to convey messages about their products and brands, directly or indirectly, to customers with the intention to:

options.a: Reduce the number of products on offer
options.b: Discourage them from comparing brands
options.c: Persuade them to purchase
options.d: Collect taxes on behalf of government

questions.explanation: This definition stresses persuasion: messages about products and brands are sent, directly or indirectly, so that customers will buy. Option B is not the stated intention, and options A and D have nothing to do with conveying brand messages.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: "The process of creating and delivering messages that promote the interests of an organisation" is a definition of:

options.a: Marketing communications
options.b: Production planning
options.c: Market research
options.d: Financial reporting

questions.explanation: Creating and delivering messages that promote an organisation's interests is one of the common definitions of marketing communications. Option C gathers information from the market rather than sending messages to it, while options B and D are operations and accounting activities.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: At its core, marketing communications encompasses the integration of all promotional tools and sources within a company in order to:

options.a: Maximise the impact on consumers and other end-users at minimal cost
options.b: Maximise the number of advertisements regardless of cost
options.c: Limit the firm's messages to only one medium
options.d: Replace the need for a product with persuasive messages

questions.explanation: This view of MarCom is about integration: combining all promotional tools so they have maximum impact on consumers and end-users at minimal cost. Option B ignores the cost side, option D wrongly suggests messages can replace the product, and option C contradicts the idea of integrating many tools.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which statement about the definition of marketing communications is correct?

options.a: It is defined only as face-to-face selling
options.b: It is defined only as television advertising
options.c: There is a single legally fixed definition used by all firms
options.d: There is no universal definition, so the subject has many interpretations

questions.explanation: To date there is no universal definition of marketing communications, which is why several interpretations exist. Option C is therefore false, and options B and A reduce MarCom to just one tool when it covers many.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: By conveying messages and information of significant value, MarCom aims to encourage audiences to offer:

options.a: Negative reviews of competitors
options.b: Neutral responses that change nothing
options.c: Positive attitudinal and behavioural responses
options.d: Lower prices for the firm's products

questions.explanation: MarCom delivers valuable messages so that audiences respond positively in both attitude (how they feel about the brand) and behaviour (what they do, such as buying). Option A is not the goal, option D confuses audience response with pricing, and option B would mean the communication failed.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Marketing communication offers answers to several questions. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

options.a: What internal and external influences affect the exchange?
options.b: How much tax should the firm pay this year?
options.c: What is being exchanged?
options.d: Who is the customer?

questions.explanation: MarCom helps answer who the customer is, what is being exchanged, and what internal and external influences affect that exchange. A firm's tax liability, option B, is a finance and accounting question, not a communication one.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The process of using words, sounds or visual cues to supply information to one or more people is a definition of:

options.a: Distribution
options.b: Pricing
options.c: Segmentation
options.d: Communication

questions.explanation: Communication is the process of using words, sound or visual cues to supply information to one or more people. Options A, C and B are other marketing activities that do not, by themselves, mean supplying information through cues.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: In simple words, the establishment of mutually satisfying exchange relationships through the buying and selling of goods, services or ideas is called:

options.a: Marketing
options.b: Auditing
options.c: Manufacturing
options.d: Accounting

questions.explanation: Marketing, in simple terms, is establishing mutually satisfying exchange relationships through buying and selling goods, services or ideas. Option C is making the goods, while options D and B record and check financial information.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Baker (2000) defines marketing as:

options.a: The act of producing goods at the lowest possible cost
options.b: The process of planning the conception, pricing, communication and distribution of ideas
options.c: A way of managing profitable customer relationships
options.d: The process of grouping homogenous consumers

questions.explanation: Baker's short definition is that marketing is a way of managing profitable customer relationships. Option B is the longer planning-and-executing definition given by Strydom, Jooste and Cant, option A is about production efficiency, and option D describes segmentation.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Kotler and Armstrong (2006) view marketing as the process through which companies create value for customers and build strong customer relationships in order to:

options.a: Capture value from customers in return
options.b: Avoid any contact with competitors
options.c: Eliminate the need for promotion
options.d: Reduce the range of customer choices

questions.explanation: This definition sees marketing as a two-way value process: firms create value for customers and build strong relationships so that they get value back in return. Options B, C and D are not part of this definition and would not explain why firms build relationships.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Stapleton and Ali note that the common definitions of marketing share some commonalities. Which of the following is NOT one of these commonalities?

options.a: A focus on reducing the number of employees
options.b: The relationship between the customer and the organisation
options.c: The provision of suitable offerings to meet customers' needs
options.d: A focus on customers

questions.explanation: The shared features are a focus on customers, suitable offerings that meet customer needs, suitable benefits to the organisation, and the customer-organisation relationship through which value is created. Cutting staff numbers, option A, is not one of them.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A customer's perception of a company or its brand is best described as:

options.a: Formed only by the price of the product
options.b: Fixed at birth and unaffected by communication
options.c: Determined only by the company's television adverts
options.d: A synthesis of bundles of messages received through many forms of communication

questions.explanation: Perception of a brand is built up from many messages together, such as advertising, price, packaging design, direct marketing, publicity, sales promotion and websites. Options C and A each pick out only one of these messages, and option B wrongly says communication has no effect.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which of the following organisations needs to communicate with a range of stakeholders?

options.a: Only manufacturing firms
options.b: Only large multinational companies
options.c: All organisations, whether commercial, government, charity or not-for-profit
options.d: Only firms that sell online

questions.explanation: Every type of organisation, large or small, commercial or government, charity, school, manufacturer or service provider, needs to communicate with stakeholders. Options B, A and D wrongly limit this need to one kind of firm.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: News distributed from a single broadcast point and made available over the airwaves or in mass print runs is an example of which type of communication?

options.a: Many-to-one
options.b: One-to-one
options.c: Many-to-many
options.d: One-to-many

questions.explanation: One-to-many communication starts from a single broadcast point and reaches a wide audience through airwaves or mass print, as in a general news announcement. Option A is the reverse flow (many replying to one), option B is a personal exchange like a sales talk, and option C is the internet pattern of everyone talking to everyone.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A bank in Lagos sends a newsletter by email, and hundreds of customers click the reply button to send their questions back to the bank. The replies illustrate which type of communication?

options.a: One-to-one
options.b: Many-to-many
options.c: Many-to-one
options.d: One-to-many

questions.explanation: Many customers sending replies to one organisation is many-to-one communication, and the email reply button is the classic example. The newsletter itself is one-to-many, option D, while options A and B describe a single personal exchange and online group conversation.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which type of communication is described as the most intensive and interactive, as in a sales presentation or a negotiation?

options.a: One-to-many
options.b: One-to-one
options.c: Many-to-one
options.d: Many-to-many

questions.explanation: One-to-one communication is the most intensive and interactive form because two parties deal directly with each other, as in a sales presentation or negotiation. Option A is a broadcast to a mass audience, option C is many replies going to one point, and option D is group interaction online.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Students of a Nigerian university swap opinions about phone brands in an online chat room and on blogs, all talking to one another at once. This illustrates:

options.a: Many-to-one communication
options.b: Many-to-many communication
options.c: One-to-one communication
options.d: One-to-many communication

questions.explanation: Many-to-many communication has grown with the highly developed internet, as in chat rooms and blogging websites where many people talk to many others. Option C involves only two parties, option D is a broadcast, and option A is many people replying to a single point.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: How many different types of communication are identified by the direction of flow between senders and receivers (one-to-many, many-to-one and so on)?

options.a: Two
options.b: Seven
options.c: Three
options.d: Four

questions.explanation: There are four types: one-to-many, many-to-one, one-to-one and many-to-many. Option B confuses this with the seven Ps of the marketing mix, and options A and C leave some of the types out.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: When a brand develops its marketing communications strategy around the marketing mix, the 'Promotion' element considers:

options.a: The people who interact with the brand's customers
options.b: Where the product is bought and sold
options.c: The pricing model used for the product
options.d: All of the ways in which the brand, product or service is communicated to the public

questions.explanation: Promotion covers every way the brand, product or service is communicated to the public, and it also involves Positioning. Option B is Place, option C is Price, and option A is People.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Within the Promotion element of the marketing mix, which additional P is used to evaluate how people view and respond to the brand?

options.a: Place
options.b: Process
options.c: Positioning
options.d: Packaging

questions.explanation: Positioning is the extra P inside Promotion that looks at how people view and respond to the brand. Option D deals with attracting customers in the physical and online marketplace, option B deals with the customer experience and communication process, and option A is where the product is sold.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: In the seven Ps marketing mix around which a brand builds its MarCom strategy, 'Process' considers:

options.a: How to attract customers in the physical and online marketplace
options.b: The customer experience and communication process
options.c: The features of the good or service
options.d: Where the good or service is bought and sold

questions.explanation: Process considers the customer experience and the communication process. Option C is Product, option D is Place, and option A is Packaging.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The marketing mix that a brand typically uses to develop its marketing communications strategy is now known as the Seven Ps. It was formerly called the:

options.a: Five forces
options.b: Four Ps
options.c: Six stages
options.d: Three Cs

questions.explanation: The Seven Ps grew out of the older Four Ps of product, price, promotion and place, which were later extended. Option A is a competition model, option D is a different framework, and option C is not a name for the marketing mix.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A Lagos fashion brand trains its shop attendants and delivery riders on how to treat customers, because they all interact with buyers. Which P of the marketing mix is this?

options.a: Product
options.b: People
options.c: Price
options.d: Place

questions.explanation: People considers everyone who interacts with a brand's customers or clients, so training attendants and riders is about People. Option A is the features of the offering, option C is the pricing model, and option D is where the goods are bought and sold.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which statement about the emergence of marketing communication is correct?

options.a: Marketing communication began only with the internet
options.b: Communication has been part of marketing for as long as people have exchanged goods
options.c: Marketing communication first appeared with social media in the 2000s
options.d: Marketing communication was invented in the 1950s with television

questions.explanation: Marketing communication is not new; communication has been part of the marketing process for as long as people have exchanged goods. Options A, D and C each confuse a later medium that made MarCom more sophisticated with the start of MarCom itself.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The advent of technology and research made marketing communication increasingly sophisticated and gave rise to:

options.a: The end of advertising
options.b: Integrated marketing communication (IMC)
options.c: The barter system
options.d: Handwritten manuscripts

questions.explanation: Technology, research and changing consumers made MarCom more sophisticated and gave rise to integrated marketing communication, where many channels deliver one unified message. Options C and D existed long before, and option A is the opposite of what happened.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The use of multiple channels to create a unified message describes:

options.a: Integrated marketing communication
options.b: Market segmentation
options.c: One-to-one communication
options.d: Personal selling

questions.explanation: Integrated marketing communication means using multiple channels together so that they deliver one unified message. Option C is a single personal exchange, option B is grouping consumers, and option D is just one tool of the mix rather than the coordination of many.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT given as a way in which consumers have changed, driving more sophisticated marketing communication?

options.a: They now have fewer choices than ever before
options.b: Their behaviour is more complex
options.c: Their media habits are different
options.d: They are more confident and outspoken

questions.explanation: Consumers have changed beyond recognition: their behaviour is more complex, their media habits differ and they are more confident and outspoken. Audiences actually have more choices than ever before, so option A states the opposite of the truth.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The invention of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg in the 15th century marked, for businesses, the birth of:

options.a: Email marketing
options.b: Television advertising
options.c: Radio commercials
options.d: Print advertising

questions.explanation: Before the printing press, information lived in handwritten manuscripts for the elite; printing made mass-produced messages possible and so gave birth to print advertising. Options B, A and C came centuries later with broadcasting and the internet.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The first printed advertisements appeared in newspapers in the:

options.a: 17th century
options.b: 20th century
options.c: 19th century
options.d: 15th century

questions.explanation: The first printed adverts appeared in 17th-century newspapers, promoting things from medicines to real estate. Option D is when Gutenberg invented the printing press, not when newspaper adverts appeared, and options C and B are too late.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Radio commercials, which gave brands a way to reach households with audio messages, began in the:
questions.explanation: Radio commercials began in the 1920s. Option B, the 1950s, is when television became the dominant platform, and option A belongs to the internet age.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: By the 1950s, which medium had emerged as the dominant platform by combining visuals and sound to create compelling advertisements?

options.a: Television
options.b: Email
options.c: Newspapers
options.d: Radio

questions.explanation: Television dominated by the 1950s because it combined pictures and sound. Option D offered sound only and started in the 1920s, option C is print, and option B came with the internet in the late 20th century.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Volkswagen's "Think Small" campaign of the 1960s is cited as showing how television could be used for:

options.a: Storytelling that fosters emotional connections with audiences
options.b: Sending replies through an email reply button
options.c: Running two-way conversations on social media
options.d: Collecting customers' email addresses

questions.explanation: "Think Small" showed that television could tell stories that build emotional connections with audiences. Options D, C and B are digital-era practices that did not exist in the 1960s.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The journey from the printing press to social media illustrates which enduring truth about marketing communication?

options.a: It has stayed the same since the 15th century
options.b: It no longer affects consumer behaviour
options.c: It is ever-evolving, so understanding its history helps firms anticipate future trends
options.d: It matters only to large firms

questions.explanation: The history shows that marketing communication is ever-evolving, and knowing that history helps businesses anticipate trends and craft strategies that resonate. Option A contradicts the evolution described, and options D and B are not supported.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Among the conditions for exchange, which one shows most directly why marketing communication is necessary?

options.a: Each must have something of value to the other
options.b: Each party can communicate and deliver what it is offering
options.c: Each party is free to accept or reject the offer
options.d: There must be at least two parties

questions.explanation: An exchange cannot happen unless each party can communicate and deliver what it offers, and this is exactly the job of marketing communication. Options D, A and C are also conditions, but they concern how many parties there are, what each one has, and freedom of choice, not communication.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: The act of obtaining a desired object from someone by offering something of value in return is called:

options.a: Publicity
options.b: Market segmentation
options.c: Brand switching
options.d: The exchange process

questions.explanation: The exchange process means getting a desired object from someone by offering something of value in return. Option B groups consumers, option A is free news coverage, and option C is customers moving from one brand to another.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Ada pays N4,500 to a Yaba bookshop and receives a textbook in return. The completed exchange between Ada and the bookshop is known as a:

options.a: Transaction
options.b: Positioning statement
options.c: Press release
options.d: Segment

questions.explanation: When an exchange between someone offering money or other resources and a company selling a good, service or idea is completed, the result is a transaction. Option D is a group of consumers, option B is about brand image, and option C is a publicity tool.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A pizza chain tells customers it delivers the newest and hottest pizza faster than rivals, in only 30 minutes. In the MarCom process, this is an example of:

options.a: Determining the unique value (selling) proposition
options.b: Allocating the budget
options.c: Developing control measures
options.d: Identifying the target audience

questions.explanation: A unique value or selling proposition (UVP or USP) is what makes a business stand out from rivals, and the 30-minute promise is the standard example. Options B and C concern money and monitoring, and option D is about choosing who to talk to, not what makes the offer special.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: In the process of marketing communications, deciding how much to spend on each channel is the stage called:

options.a: Selecting channels
options.b: Execution
options.c: Budget allocation
options.d: Message development

questions.explanation: Budget allocation answers the question of how much to spend on each channel. Option D is crafting the key messages, option B is implementing the plan, and option A picks which channels to use but not how much each gets.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: In the MarCom process, measuring a campaign's effectiveness against objectives and making the necessary adjustments is called:

options.a: Developing control measures
options.b: Message development
options.c: Bringing the solution to customers' queries
options.d: Identifying the target audience

questions.explanation: Developing control measures means checking the campaign's effectiveness against its objectives and adjusting where needed. Option B is writing the messages, option D is the very first stage, and option C is about addressing customers' pain points.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: In the process of marketing communications, the channels a firm uses to deliver its brand message should depend on:

options.a: The personal hobbies of the marketing manager
options.b: Only the cheapest channel available
options.c: The objectives it wants to accomplish and its customers' preferences
options.d: Whatever channel its competitors used last year

questions.explanation: Channel choice depends on the objectives the firm wants to accomplish and on its customers' preferences. Options D, B and A ignore both of these and would waste the message on the wrong medium.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: What is the primary objective of marketing communications?

options.a: To cut production costs
options.b: To reduce the number of competitors by law
options.c: To avoid customer feedback
options.d: To increase sales volume through persuasive, informative and positive messages

questions.explanation: The primary objective of marketing communications is to increase sales volume through persuasive, informative and positive messages; the other objectives support this. Options B and A are not communication goals, and option C goes against the interactive nature of MarCom.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: How are marketing communication objectives described in terms of time frame?

options.a: As goals that apply only on a product's launch day
options.b: As daily targets that are dropped after one week
options.c: As objectives with no link to brand value
options.d: As long-term goals that aim to boost the brand's value over time

questions.explanation: Marketing communication objectives are long-term goals through which marketing strategies aim to boost the brand's value over time. Options B and A make them short-lived, and option C removes the link to brand value.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A new fintech company has just entered the Nigerian market and runs radio commercials and print ads so that people know the business and its app exist. Which MarCom objective is it pursuing?

options.a: Drive brand switching
options.b: Increase brand awareness
options.c: Stimulate repeat patronage
options.d: Change attitudes

questions.explanation: When a firm first enters a market, people need to know that it and its offerings exist, so it broadcasts commercials or print ads to increase brand awareness. Option A targets rivals' customers, option C targets people who have already bought, and option D corrects mistaken beliefs.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: False rumours spread that a Nigerian bottled-water brand is unsafe, so the firm runs a campaign showing its NAFDAC approval and factory tests. Which MarCom objective does this campaign serve?

options.a: Stimulate trial purchase
options.b: Conduct research for the company
options.c: Increase brand awareness
options.d: Change attitudes

questions.explanation: Changing attitudes means altering views of a product or brand, especially when mistaken beliefs have spread in the market. Option C is about letting people know a brand exists, which they already do here, option A is getting first-time use, and option B is reading market trends.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A cosmetics firm in Lagos hands out free sample sachets of a new cream at a mall so that shoppers can try it without risk. Which objective is it mainly pursuing?

options.a: Stimulate trial purchase
options.b: Conduct research for the company
options.c: Change attitudes
options.d: Build a brand image over a long period

questions.explanation: Free trials or samples are popular ways to get consumers to try a product first, taking the risk off and letting them experience the brand. Option C corrects false beliefs, option B reads market trends, and option D is a long-term goal not specific to sampling.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A telecom company offers bonus data to customers of rival networks who port their lines to it. Which MarCom objective does this target?

options.a: Drive brand switching
options.b: Conduct research for the company
options.c: Change attitudes
options.d: Increase brand awareness

questions.explanation: Driving brand switching aims to get customers who buy competing products to move to your brand. Option D only makes people aware a brand exists, option B studies the market, and option C corrects mistaken beliefs, none of which directly pulls rivals' customers across.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Influencing purchase intent is typically achieved by compelling adverts that generally focus on:

options.a: The company's internal staff structure
options.b: The firm's tax payments
options.c: The superior benefits to users compared to competitors
options.d: The history of the printing press

questions.explanation: Ads that influence purchase intent usually stress the superior benefits users get compared with competitors' products. Options A, D and B would not motivate a customer to buy.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a specific objective of marketing communications?

options.a: Building a brand image
options.b: Conducting research for the company
options.c: Doing direct selling
options.d: Fixing the company's production machinery

questions.explanation: The specific objectives include awareness, changing attitudes, purchase intent, trial and repeat purchase, brand switching, connecting companies with consumers, building brand image, conducting research and direct selling. Maintaining machinery, option D, is a production task.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: When marketing communications 'conducts research for the company', it is expected to:

options.a: Write the company's annual financial statements
options.b: Connect company stakeholders with the market by reading trend movements in the sector
options.c: Recruit new staff for the company
options.d: Design the factory layout

questions.explanation: Some MarCom work links company stakeholders with the market, so marketers must read trend movements in the firm's sector. Options A, D and C belong to finance, operations and human resources.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the important roles of marketing communications?

options.a: Shortening the sales cycle
options.b: Setting the legal minimum wage
options.c: Building brand awareness
options.d: Maintaining customer loyalty

questions.explanation: The key roles are building brand awareness, maintaining customer loyalty, creating demand, shortening the sales cycle and highlighting a competitive edge. Setting a minimum wage, option B, is a government function.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Marketing communications can shorten the sales cycle by:

options.a: Removing all information about the product
options.b: Better understanding customer needs, motivations, influences and buying processes and using this insight when engaging consumers
options.c: Raising prices so that fewer people buy
options.d: Delaying responses to customer enquiries

questions.explanation: The sales cycle gets shorter when the firm understands customer needs, buying motivations, influences and processes and uses that insight when engaging consumers. Options A, C and D would slow down or block buying decisions.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Why is highlighting a competitive edge an important role of marketing communications?

options.a: Because competitors are not allowed to advertise
options.b: In a crowded marketplace, the points that make a product unique must be shared with the public
options.c: Because products no longer differ from one another
options.d: Because customers dislike learning about product features

questions.explanation: The 21st-century marketplace is crowded, so MarCom must share the points of differentiation that make products unique and so strengthen competitive advantage. Option C contradicts the idea of differentiation, and options A and D are untrue.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: "It is not enough to have improved or innovative goods or services; people need to know they exist in order to buy them." This statement explains which role of marketing communications?

options.a: Shortening the sales cycle
options.b: Conducting research for the company
options.c: Creating demand for products and services
options.d: Maintaining customer loyalty

questions.explanation: Creating demand depends on people knowing that a product exists, however good or innovative it is. Option D is about keeping an existing positive bond, option A is about speeding up buying, and option B is reading market trends.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A supermarket chain in Abuja sends birthday messages and loyalty-point updates to regular shoppers to keep a positive bond with them. Which role of MarCom is this?

options.a: Building brand awareness
options.b: Maintaining customer loyalty
options.c: Highlighting a competitive edge
options.d: Creating demand for new products

questions.explanation: Maintaining customer loyalty is about making sure existing customers keep a positive bond with the company and its brands. Option A targets people who do not yet know the firm, option C stresses what makes it different from rivals, and option D is about getting people to want a new offering.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: Besides the main roles, marketing communications has other specific roles. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

options.a: Integrating all marketing tools to achieve seamless communication
options.b: Engaging customers at various points along the buying journey
options.c: Influencing consumer behaviour to drive sales
options.d: Replacing the need for a quality product

questions.explanation: The other specific roles are influencing consumer behaviour to drive sales, engaging customers along the buying journey and integrating all marketing tools for seamless communication. Communication supports a good product but cannot replace it, so option D is not a role.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: In the DRIP framework for the roles of marketing communications, the letters D, R, I and P stand for:

options.a: Demand, Reach, Image, Profit
options.b: Design, Research, Implement, Plan
options.c: Differentiate, Reinforce, Inform, Persuade
options.d: Distribute, Retail, Invest, Price

questions.explanation: DRIP sums up the four roles of MarCom: to Differentiate an offering from rivals, Reinforce earlier messages and experiences, Inform audiences, and Persuade them to act. Options D, B and A are made-up expansions mixing other business terms.

questions.topic: Nature, Types, Roles and Objectives of Marketing Communication
questions.question: A popular Nigerian beverage brand that everyone already knows keeps running adverts reminding loyal buyers of the good experiences they have had with it. Under the DRIP roles, this mainly serves to:

options.a: Differentiate
options.b: Inform
options.c: Reinforce
options.d: Persuade

questions.explanation: Reinforcing means reminding customers and confirming the benefits and positive experiences they have already had, which keeps existing buyers loyal. Option B gives new information to people who lack it, option A sets the brand apart from rivals, and option D pushes people towards a new action or attitude.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A basic model of the marketing communication process typically includes:

options.a: Product, price, place and promotion
options.b: Sender, encoded message, medium, receiver and feedback
options.c: Segmentation, targeting and positioning
options.d: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats

questions.explanation: A communication model shows how a sender encodes a message, sends it through a medium to a receiver who decodes it, and then gets feedback. Option A is the marketing mix, C is the process for choosing target markets, and D is a SWOT analysis used in planning, so none of them describes how a message travels.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: The Marketing Communications Planning Framework (MCPF) is designed to:

options.a: Provide a structured approach for aligning communication strategies with business objectives
options.b: Calculate the unit cost of producing each product
options.c: Replace the need to set communication objectives
options.d: Decide the physical design of the product

questions.explanation: The MCPF gives planners an orderly sequence, from analysing the context and setting objectives to implementing and evaluating, so that communication supports the firm's goals. Option C is wrong because objective setting is part of the framework itself, while B and D are costing and product design tasks.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: The development of an effective marketing communications plan requires:

options.a: Setting measurable goals, selecting appropriate tools and evaluating outcomes
options.b: Choosing media first and setting objectives only after the campaign ends
options.c: Copying a competitor's plan without analysing the target audience
options.d: Spending the budget equally on every available promotional tool

questions.explanation: A good plan starts with clear, measurable objectives, picks the tools that suit the audience and those objectives, and checks results afterwards. Option B reverses the logical order, C skips the audience analysis that the plan depends on, and D ignores the fact that tools should be chosen according to objectives and audience.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In the process of marketing communications, the first stage is to:

options.a: Determine the company's unique value proposition
options.b: Select the channels to deliver the brand message
options.c: Allocate the budget to each channel
options.d: Identify the target audience

questions.explanation: Presenting an offer to everyone does not work, so the process begins by deciding exactly who the messages are for. Options A, B and C are real stages, but they come later, because the value proposition, channels and budget all depend on knowing the audience first.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: Domino's Pizza positioning itself as the business that delivers the newest and hottest pizza faster than competitors, in only 30 minutes, is an example of a firm's:

options.a: Unique value (selling) proposition
options.b: Target audience
options.c: Budget allocation
options.d: Control measure

questions.explanation: A unique value or selling proposition is what makes a business stand out and outperform rivals, and the 30-minute hot pizza promise is exactly that. Option B is the group of people the firm is talking to, C is how much is spent on each channel, and D is how results are checked against objectives.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A sound marketing communication model underscores the significance of:

options.a: Feedback as a way of refining the effectiveness of messages
options.b: One-way transmission with no response from the receiver
options.c: Choosing the medium only after the message has been received
options.d: Ignoring how the receiver interprets the message

questions.explanation: Feedback is the receiver's response, and it tells the sender whether the message was understood and acted on, so the next message can be improved. Option B describes a model with no feedback at all, C gets the order of the process wrong, and D ignores decoding, which is central to whether communication works.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In the Marketing Communications Planning Framework (MCPF), which element comes first?

options.a: Context analysis
options.b: Evaluation and control
options.c: Scheduling and implementation
options.d: Allocation of resources (budget)

questions.explanation: Planning starts by analysing the context, that is the customers, the business, the organisation and the wider environment, because every later decision depends on that understanding. Option B is the final stage, and C and D come after objectives and strategy have been set.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A well-executed marketing communications plan ensures:

options.a: That each promotional tool sends a different, unrelated message
options.b: That only one promotional tool is ever used
options.c: Integration and consistency across all communication touchpoints
options.d: That evaluation becomes unnecessary once the campaign is launched

questions.explanation: Planning brings the different tools together so that customers get one clear, consistent message wherever they meet the brand. Option A is the opposite of integration, B is wrong because plans usually combine several tools, and D is wrong because evaluation and control are part of every plan.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: The usefulness of a marketing communication model lies in its ability to:

options.a: Set the selling price of the product
options.b: Forecast the firm's production output
options.c: Replace the need for audience research
options.d: Explain how persuasive messages are transmitted and received

questions.explanation: A communication model maps the journey of a message from sender to receiver and back through feedback, which helps marketers see where communication can succeed or break down. Option A is a pricing decision, B is a production planning task, and C is wrong because the model actually highlights how much the receiver matters.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In the Marketing Communications Planning Framework (MCPF), which element comes last?

options.a: Context analysis
options.b: Setting communication objectives
options.c: Formulating the marketing communications strategy
options.d: Evaluation and control

questions.explanation: After a plan has been implemented, the results are measured against the objectives and adjustments are made, which is why evaluation and control close the framework. Option A is the starting point, and B and C are early planning steps that come before resources, scheduling and implementation.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A foundational element of a marketing communications plan is:

options.a: Choosing the cheapest medium regardless of the audience
options.b: Leaving objectives undefined to allow flexibility
options.c: Repeating the previous year's plan unchanged
options.d: Formulating precise, actionable and time-bound objectives

questions.explanation: Clear, measurable and time-bound objectives guide every other choice in the plan and make it possible to evaluate results. Option B removes that foundation, A ignores the audience, and C ignores changes in the market and in the firm's goals.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: Which sequence correctly shows the basic communication process?

options.a: Receiver - encoding - medium - decoding - sender - feedback
options.b: Sender - decoding - medium - encoding - receiver - feedback
options.c: Sender - feedback - medium - encoding - receiver - decoding
options.d: Sender - encoding - medium - decoding - receiver - feedback

questions.explanation: The sender first encodes the idea into a message, sends it through a medium, the receiver decodes it, and the receiver's response travels back as feedback. Option B swaps encoding and decoding, A puts the receiver at the start, and C places feedback before the message has even been received.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A model that shows communication as a one-way flow from a sender, through encoding, a message and a channel, to decoding by a receiver is called:

options.a: The two-step flow model
options.b: The innovation-adoption model
options.c: The AIDA model
options.d: The linear model of communication

questions.explanation: The linear model shows communication moving in one direction from sender to receiver through encoding, message, channel and decoding, with feedback and noise added in later versions. Option A is about media influence passing through opinion leaders, while options C and B are hierarchy-of-effects models of buyer response.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In the communication process, 'encoding' means:

options.a: The receiver interpreting the message
options.b: Anything that distorts the message
options.c: The medium that carries the message
options.d: Turning the sender's ideas into a message made of words, pictures, symbols or sounds

questions.explanation: Encoding is the sender's job of putting an idea into a form that can be sent, such as words, images, symbols or sounds. Option A is decoding, option C is the channel or medium, and option B is noise.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In the communication process, 'decoding' refers to:

options.a: Interference that disrupts the message
options.b: The sender converting ideas into symbols
options.c: The sender choosing which medium to use
options.d: The receiver interpreting the symbols in a message to give it meaning

questions.explanation: Decoding is the receiver's work of interpreting the words, images or sounds and assigning meaning to them. Option C is a channel decision, option B is encoding, and option A is noise.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: Any unplanned interference or distortion in the communication process that stops the receiver getting the message as intended is called:

options.a: Encoding
options.b: Field of experience
options.c: Noise
options.d: Feedback

questions.explanation: Noise is any unplanned distortion or interference, such as a poor network signal or competing adverts, that prevents the message being received as intended. Option D is the receiver's response, option A is the sender putting ideas into symbols, and option B is the experience each party brings.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: After hearing a radio jingle for a new noodle brand, a listener calls the toll-free line to ask where to buy it. In the communication model, the call is an example of:

options.a: The channel
options.b: Noise
options.c: Encoding
options.d: Feedback

questions.explanation: Feedback is the part of the receiver's response that goes back to the sender, and a phone call asking where to buy is a direct example. Option C is done by the sender, option B is interference, and option A is the radio itself.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In Schramm's model of communication, the 'field of experience' refers to:

options.a: The budget available for the campaign
options.b: The number of times an advert is broadcast
options.c: The physical room where an advert is shown
options.d: The experiences, attitudes and perceptions that sender and receiver bring, with understanding greatest where they overlap

questions.explanation: Each party brings its own experiences, values and perceptions to the process, and communication works best where the sender's and receiver's fields of experience overlap. Options C, B and A are a place, a frequency and a budget, not shared understanding.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A Lagos bank uses slang and references that its young target customers in Ibadan do not understand, so the advert fails. In Schramm's terms, the failure is mainly due to:

options.a: Too much feedback from the receiver
options.b: Encoding the message in a shared language
options.c: Choosing a medium with no noise
options.d: Too little overlap between the fields of experience of sender and receiver

questions.explanation: When sender and receiver share little experience, the receiver cannot decode the symbols as intended, so the message fails. Option A would help, not harm, option C describes an ideal situation, and option B would increase understanding.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A key weakness of the basic linear model of communication is that it:

options.a: Applies only to personal selling
options.b: Treats communication as a one-way process with a passive receiver
options.c: Ignores the sender completely
options.d: Includes too many opinion leaders

questions.explanation: The basic linear model shows messages flowing one way to a passive receiver, which understates how audiences interpret, respond and talk back, especially in the digital age. Options D, C and A are not features of the linear model.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A model in which messages flow from the mass media to opinion leaders, who then pass them on to opinion followers, is the:

options.a: AIDA model
options.b: DAGMAR model
options.c: One-step (hypodermic) model
options.d: Two-step flow model

questions.explanation: In the two-step flow model, information passes first from the media to opinion leaders and then by word of mouth from those leaders to their followers. Option C assumes the media reach audiences directly with no go-between, and options A and B are hierarchy-of-effects models.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: How does the one-step flow model of communication differ from the two-step flow model?

options.a: The one-step model includes feedback while the two-step model does not
options.b: The one-step model has six stages of buyer response
options.c: In the one-step model opinion leaders are the only source of information
options.d: In the one-step model the media reach the audience directly, with no opinion leaders in between

questions.explanation: The one-step (or hypodermic) model assumes mass media messages go straight to the target audience and affect it directly, while the two-step model adds opinion leaders as go-betweens. Option C gets the models the wrong way round, and options A and B describe other ideas.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A skincare brand sends free products to a well-known Nigerian beauty blogger, hoping her followers will copy her recommendations. Which communication model does this strategy rely on most?

options.a: The one-step flow model
options.b: The innovation-adoption model
options.c: The two-step flow model
options.d: The DAGMAR model

questions.explanation: The brand is targeting an opinion leader who will pass the message on to her followers, which is the core idea of two-step flow. Option A would mean advertising straight to consumers, and options D and B describe response stages rather than how influence travels.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: The multi-step flow model develops the two-step model by recognising that:

options.a: Messages always reach consumers in a single step
options.b: Information can flow in several directions among the media, opinion leaders and opinion followers
options.c: Only the sender can influence the receiver
options.d: Opinion leaders never use the media

questions.explanation: Multi-step flow accepts that information moves among media, opinion leaders, opinion formers and followers in several directions, and that followers can also get messages directly. Options D, C and A contradict the model.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: Models that assume buyers pass through a set sequence of stages, from awareness to purchase, in response to marketing communication are called:

options.a: Market segmentation models
options.b: Hierarchy-of-effects (response hierarchy) models
options.c: Pricing models
options.d: Distribution channel models

questions.explanation: Hierarchy-of-effects models, such as AIDA and Lavidge and Steiner's model, assume people move step by step from first noticing a brand to buying it. Options D, C and A cover other areas of marketing.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: The letters in the AIDA model stand for:

options.a: Attention, Image, Demand, Advocacy
options.b: Attention, Interest, Desire, Action
options.c: Analysis, Implementation, Direction, Assessment
options.d: Awareness, Information, Decision, Adoption

questions.explanation: AIDA describes the stages a buyer goes through: Attention, then Interest, then Desire, then Action. Options D, A and C swap in words from other models or planning steps.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In the AIDA model, which stage comes immediately after Interest?

options.a: Attention
options.b: Desire
options.c: Awareness
options.d: Action

questions.explanation: The sequence is Attention, Interest, Desire, Action, so Desire follows Interest. Option A comes before Interest, option D is the final stage after Desire, and option C is a stage in other models, not a letter in AIDA.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A poster for a new Lagos gym uses bright colours and a bold headline so that passers-by stop and look at it. Which AIDA stage is the design mainly aimed at?

options.a: Action
options.b: Desire
options.c: Interest
options.d: Attention

questions.explanation: Attention is the first AIDA stage: before anything else, the message must be noticed, which is what bold colours and headlines do. Option C comes when the viewer wants to learn more, option B when they want the product, and option A when they sign up.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: An online store's advert ends with a "Shop now - offer ends at midnight" button. Which AIDA stage is this mainly aimed at?

options.a: Attention
options.b: Desire
options.c: Action
options.d: Interest

questions.explanation: Action is the final AIDA stage, where the buyer is pushed to act, for example by clicking to buy before a deadline. Options A, D and B are earlier stages about getting noticed, holding curiosity and creating a want.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: DAGMAR stands for:

options.a: Designing Advertisements to Gain Market Access and Revenue
options.b: Direct Advertising Generates More Average Returns
options.c: Defining Advertising Goals for Measured Advertising Results
options.d: Developing Annual Goals for Marketing and Retail

questions.explanation: DAGMAR means Defining Advertising Goals for Measured Advertising Results, an approach that says advertising goals should be clear and measurable. The other expansions in options A, B and D are invented.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: The DAGMAR approach to setting advertising objectives was developed by:

options.a: Everett Rogers
options.b: E. St. Elmo Lewis
options.c: Lavidge and Steiner
options.d: Russell Colley

questions.explanation: Russell Colley proposed DAGMAR in 1961 for the Association of National Advertisers. Option C produced the six-stage hierarchy of effects, option B is linked with AIDA, and option A with the diffusion and adoption of innovations.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In the DAGMAR model, the communication stages a consumer passes through are:

options.a: Attention, interest, desire, action
options.b: Awareness, knowledge, liking, preference, conviction, purchase
options.c: Awareness, comprehension, conviction, action
options.d: Awareness, interest, evaluation, trial, adoption

questions.explanation: DAGMAR's communication spectrum runs from awareness to comprehension to conviction and finally action. Option A is AIDA, option B is Lavidge and Steiner's model, and option D is the innovation-adoption model.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: A central principle of DAGMAR is that advertising objectives should be:

options.a: Specific and measurable, with a defined target audience, benchmark, degree of change and time period
options.b: Expressed only as total sales revenue
options.c: Set after the campaign has ended
options.d: Kept vague so that they can never be missed

questions.explanation: DAGMAR says a good advertising objective is a specific, measurable communication task, stating the target audience, a starting benchmark, the degree of change wanted and the time period. Option D makes results impossible to measure, option B ignores that advertising's effect on sales is hard to isolate, and option C reverses the planning order.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: Lavidge and Steiner's hierarchy-of-effects model has six stages. Which sequence is correct?

options.a: Awareness, knowledge, liking, preference, conviction, purchase
options.b: Attention, interest, desire, conviction, preference, action
options.c: Awareness, liking, knowledge, conviction, preference, purchase
options.d: Knowledge, awareness, preference, liking, purchase, conviction

questions.explanation: Lavidge and Steiner's steps are awareness, knowledge, liking, preference, conviction and purchase. Options C and D put the right words in the wrong order, and option B mixes in AIDA terms.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In Lavidge and Steiner's model, liking and preference belong to which component of attitude?

options.a: Physical (sensory)
options.b: Conative (behavioural)
options.c: Affective (feeling)
options.d: Cognitive (thinking)

questions.explanation: Liking and preference are about feelings towards the brand, so they form the affective stage. Option D covers awareness and knowledge, option B covers conviction and purchase, and option A is not one of the three components.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In hierarchy-of-effects models, the cognitive stage refers to:

options.a: What the receiver knows or thinks, such as awareness and knowledge
options.b: What the receiver feels, such as liking
options.c: What the receiver does, such as buying
options.d: How much the sender spends on media

questions.explanation: The cognitive stage is the thinking or knowing stage, covering awareness and knowledge of the brand. Option B is the affective (feeling) stage, option C is the conative (behaviour) stage, and option D is a budget matter.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: The conative stage of a response hierarchy refers to:

options.a: The liking stage
options.b: The awareness stage
options.c: The noise in the channel
options.d: The behaviour or action stage, such as trial and purchase

questions.explanation: Conative means action or behaviour, so it covers stages like conviction, trial and purchase. Option B is cognitive, option A is affective, and option C is a communication-model element.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: The innovation-adoption model describes the stages a consumer goes through in accepting a new product as:

options.a: Awareness, interest, evaluation, trial, adoption
options.b: Awareness, comprehension, conviction, action
options.c: Exposure, reception, cognitive response, behaviour
options.d: Attention, interest, desire, action

questions.explanation: The innovation-adoption model moves from awareness and interest through evaluation and trial to adoption of a new product. Option D is AIDA, option B is DAGMAR, and option C is the information-processing model.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: Which is a common criticism of hierarchy-of-effects models?

options.a: They ignore purchase as an outcome
options.b: Consumers do not always pass through the stages in a fixed order; for example, impulse purchases may come before strong attitudes form
options.c: They can only be used for radio advertising
options.d: They pay no attention to awareness

questions.explanation: Critics argue the stages are not always linear: with low-involvement or impulse buys, people may purchase first and form attitudes afterwards. Options D and A are wrong because awareness and purchase are central to these models, and option C has no basis.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: Why is a marketing communications plan needed?

options.a: It sets out in a logical order what the firm wants to achieve with communication and how, so activities are coordinated and can be evaluated
options.b: It replaces the overall marketing plan
options.c: It removes the need to set objectives
options.d: It guarantees that every campaign will succeed

questions.explanation: A MarCom plan brings order and integration: it links objectives, strategy, tools, timing, budget and evaluation so that activities work together and results can be judged. Option C contradicts planning itself, option D overclaims, and option B is wrong because the MarCom plan comes from the marketing plan.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: The Marketing Communications Planning Framework (MCPF) is best described as:

options.a: A list of all television stations in a country
options.b: A model of how opinion leaders influence followers
options.c: A sequence of linked stages that guides the development of a marketing communications plan
options.d: A financial statement showing advertising costs

questions.explanation: The MCPF is a framework of linked stages, from context analysis to evaluation, that helps managers build a marketing communications plan in a logical, integrated way. Option A is a media list, option D is accounting, and option B is the two-step flow model.

questions.topic: Models of Marketing Communication and MarCom Planning
questions.question: In the MCPF, which stage comes immediately after the context analysis?

options.a: Control and evaluation
options.b: Setting communication objectives
options.c: Scheduling and implementation
options.d: Allocating resources
