questions.question: Why is word-of-mouth usually seen as more credible than advertising?

options.a: It is always more detailed than advertising
options.b: It comes from people who are seen as independent of the firm and not paid to promote the product
options.c: It is controlled and checked by the company before it is shared
options.d: It always reaches more people than advertising

questions.explanation: Consumers trust friends, family and fellow customers because they are not seen as having a commercial interest in the sale. WOM is not controlled by the firm (option C), and it does not always reach more people than advertising (option D).

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) is best defined as:

options.a: Banner adverts placed by a firm on websites
options.b: Positive or negative statements by potential, actual or former customers about a product or company, made available to many people through the internet
options.c: Phone calls between a salesperson and a customer
options.d: Emails sent by a company to its mailing list

questions.explanation: eWOM is word-of-mouth that happens online, through reviews, posts, comments and forums, and it can be seen by many people. Options D and A are messages controlled and sent by the firm, and option C is personal selling.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Compared with traditional word-of-mouth, electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM):

options.a: Disappears as soon as the conversation ends
options.b: Takes place only face to face between close friends
options.c: Can reach many more people faster and stays available online for a long time
options.d: Can only be positive about a brand

questions.explanation: Traditional WOM is usually spoken between a few people and is quickly forgotten, while eWOM can spread to thousands, even strangers, within hours and remains searchable. Options B and A describe traditional WOM, and eWOM can be positive or negative (option D).

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Before buying a blender on an online store, Amaka reads 40 customer reviews and star ratings posted by previous buyers. These reviews are an example of:

options.a: Personal selling
options.b: Direct marketing
options.c: Publicity
options.d: Electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM)

questions.explanation: Reviews and ratings posted online by customers are a common form of eWOM, since they are consumers' opinions shared through the internet. Option C, publicity, is unpaid coverage in the news media, and option B is personalised communication sent by the firm to individuals.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: A customer posts a video complaint on X about poor service at a bank branch in Ikeja. Within a day it is shared thousands of times and the bank's name is trending. This mainly shows which risk of social media?

options.a: Negative eWOM can spread quickly and damage reputation
options.b: High printing costs
options.c: Slow delivery of messages
options.d: Lack of any audience on social media

questions.explanation: Social media lets dissatisfied customers reach huge audiences very quickly, so one complaint can become a reputation problem. Social media has no printing costs (option B), and the fast spread shows a large audience (option D) and speedy delivery (option C).

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: A social media influencer is best described as:

options.a: A person who has built a following online and can affect the opinions and purchases of that audience
options.b: Any customer who buys a product online
options.c: A government official who regulates advertising
options.d: A company's head of production

questions.explanation: Influencers are content creators with an engaged online following whose recommendations can shape their followers' attitudes and buying decisions. Simply buying online (option B) does not make someone an influencer, and options D and C are roles that do not depend on an online following.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Compared with celebrity (mega) influencers, micro-influencers typically have:

options.a: Audiences that never interact with their posts
options.b: No followers at all
options.c: Much larger audiences and much higher fees
options.d: Smaller, more specialised audiences and often higher engagement and trust

questions.explanation: Micro-influencers have smaller, niche followings, and their followers often see them as relatable, so engagement and trust tend to be high. Option C describes mega or celebrity influencers, and options B and A contradict the idea of an influencer.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: A small Abuja skincare brand has N200,000 to spend on influencers. It wants believable recommendations to women who follow skincare content closely. The most suitable approach is to:

options.a: Spend the entire budget on a TV commercial
options.b: Avoid social media and print flyers only
options.c: Pay one celebrity musician for a single post
options.d: Work with several micro-influencers who focus on skincare

questions.explanation: Micro-influencers in a niche such as skincare are affordable, trusted by their followers and reach exactly the target audience. A top celebrity (option C) would probably cost more than the budget and reach many people outside the target, and option A is not influencer marketing at all.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Why should an influencer clearly disclose when a post is a paid partnership with a brand?

options.a: So that the brand can avoid paying the influencer
options.b: Because paid posts cannot contain pictures
options.c: So that followers know it is advertising and are not misled
options.d: So that the post reaches fewer people

questions.explanation: Disclosure (for example marking a post as an ad or paid partnership) is about honesty: followers have a right to know when content is sponsored. Hidden sponsorship can mislead consumers and damage trust in both the influencer and the brand. Options D, B and A are not reasons for disclosure.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: In the paid-owned-earned media framework, 'earned media' refers to:

options.a: The salary earned by a firm's marketing staff
options.b: Publicity and exposure gained free through customers, fans and the press sharing or talking about the brand
options.c: Channels the firm controls, such as its own website and social media pages
options.d: Media space a firm buys, such as sponsored posts

questions.explanation: Earned media is exposure the brand earns rather than pays for, such as shares, reviews, word-of-mouth and news coverage. Option D is paid media and option C is owned media.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of owned media?

options.a: A sponsored post bought on Facebook
options.b: A newspaper story about the company
options.c: A company's official website and Instagram page
options.d: A customer's review on a blog

questions.explanation: Owned media are channels the firm itself controls, such as its website, app and official social media accounts. Option A is paid media, while options D and B are earned media because the firm did not create or pay for them.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of paid media?

options.a: A free news story about a product launch
options.b: Customers sharing a brand's video for free
options.c: A boosted (sponsored) Instagram post
options.d: A firm's own blog

questions.explanation: Paid media is exposure the firm pays for, such as boosted posts, search ads and display ads. Option D is owned media, and options B and A are earned media.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: After many customers praised a new Lagos fintech app on social media, a national newspaper wrote a free feature story about it. The newspaper story is best classified as:

options.a: Owned media
options.b: Personal selling
options.c: Earned media
options.d: Paid media

questions.explanation: The fintech did not pay for the story or control the newspaper, so the coverage is earned media. Option D would apply only if the firm had bought the space, and option A covers the firm's own channels such as its website.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Buzz marketing involves:

options.a: Cutting prices temporarily to clear stock
options.b: Getting opinion leaders and early users talking about a product so that excitement spreads to others
options.c: Sending catalogues to a mailing list
options.d: Running loud adverts at a high volume on radio

questions.explanation: Buzz marketing deliberately creates excitement by involving opinion leaders or enthusiastic customers who then spread the word in their communities. Option D takes 'buzz' literally, option A is sales promotion, and option C is direct marketing.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Deliberately giving a new product or piece of content to selected well-connected people first, so that they will share it with their networks, is called:

options.a: Encoding
options.b: Rebating
options.c: Seeding
options.d: Segmentation

questions.explanation: Seeding places content or products with chosen people who are likely to pass them on, and it is commonly used to start viral and word-of-mouth campaigns. Option D is dividing a market into groups, and option B is a sales promotion refund.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Social listening refers to:

options.a: Holding telephone interviews with job applicants
options.b: Listening to radio adverts on a smartphone
options.c: Playing music in the background of social media videos
options.d: Monitoring online conversations to learn what people are saying about a brand, its competitors and its industry

questions.explanation: Social listening means tracking mentions, comments and hashtags across social media and the web to understand opinions and spot problems or opportunities early. Options C, B and A involve sound or listening but have nothing to do with tracking online conversations.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Which of the following is a measure of engagement on social media?

options.a: The firm's annual electricity bill
options.b: The number of staff in the finance department
options.c: The size of the firm's office
options.d: The number of likes, comments and shares on a post

questions.explanation: Engagement measures how actively people interact with content, through likes, comments, shares and saves. Options C, B and A are internal business facts that say nothing about audience interaction.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: On social media, how does 'reach' differ from 'impressions'?

options.a: Reach counts only shares, while impressions counts only comments
options.b: Reach and impressions always give exactly the same figure
options.c: Reach is the number of times content was displayed, while impressions is the number of different people who saw it
options.d: Reach is the number of different people who saw the content, while impressions is the total number of times it was displayed

questions.explanation: Reach counts unique viewers, while impressions count every display, so one person seeing a post three times adds one to reach and three to impressions. Option C reverses the two terms, and option B is wrong because impressions are usually higher than reach.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of social media for marketing communication?

options.a: It guarantees that every customer will say only good things
options.b: It allows precise targeting of audiences at relatively low cost
options.c: It works only for very large companies
options.d: It removes the need for any marketing planning

questions.explanation: Social media lets firms target people by location, interests and demographics, often for far less than traditional mass media. It does not control what customers say (option A), still needs planning (option D), and is widely used by small businesses (option C).

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of social media marketing?

options.a: Ability to measure responses such as clicks and shares
options.b: Quick, real-time feedback
options.c: Direct two-way interaction with customers
options.d: Full control over what customers say about the brand

questions.explanation: On social media customers say what they like, so firms lose some control over the conversation; this is a risk, not an advantage. Two-way interaction (option C), real-time feedback (option B) and measurability (option A) are genuine advantages.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: A major risk for brands using social media is that:

options.a: They have less control over the message, because customers can comment, share and change its meaning
options.b: Their messages can never reach young people
options.c: Customers cannot respond to brand posts
options.d: Social media does not allow pictures or videos

questions.explanation: Once a brand posts content, customers can reply, criticise, remix and share it, so the final meaning is shaped by the audience as well as the brand. Social media is popular with young people (option B), supports pictures and video (option D), and is built for customer responses (option C).

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Creating fake reviews or fake 'ordinary customer' accounts to make it look as if there is genuine public support for a product is known as:

options.a: Seeding
options.b: Astroturfing
options.c: Social listening
options.d: Owned media

questions.explanation: Astroturfing is a deceptive practice that disguises paid or company-made messages as spontaneous grassroots opinion. Seeding (option A) openly gives content to real people to share, and social listening (option C) is monitoring conversations, not faking them.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: A brand launches a hashtag inviting customers to share happy memories with its product. Instead, many people use the hashtag to post complaints about poor quality. This illustrates:

options.a: Hashtag hijacking, a risk of losing control of a social media campaign
options.b: Sales promotion through coupons
options.c: Use of owned media to control the message
options.d: Successful seeding of positive content

questions.explanation: When users take over a brand's hashtag to push their own, often negative, messages, the campaign is said to be hijacked, which shows how little control brands have on social media. Options D and C wrongly suggest the brand kept control, and option B involves no incentive.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: A Lagos bakery posts two new cake flavours on Instagram in the morning. By evening, hundreds of comments show customers prefer one flavour, so the bakery decides to produce more of it. This shows which advantage of social media?

options.a: Real-time customer feedback
options.b: Higher printing costs
options.c: One-way communication
options.d: Complete control over customer opinions

questions.explanation: Social media gives firms quick feedback from customers, which they can use to adjust products and messages. Option C is wrong because the comments show two-way communication, and option D is wrong because customers freely gave their own opinions.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: The ongoing activity of building and managing relationships with a brand's online followers, such as replying to comments and answering questions, is called:

options.a: Community management
options.b: Publicity
options.c: Market segmentation
options.d: Personal selling

questions.explanation: Community management covers the daily interaction a brand has with its online audience, such as replying, moderating discussions and building loyalty. Option D is face-to-face selling by a sales force, and option B is unpaid coverage in the news media.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Loyal customers who voluntarily recommend a brand to others and defend it online, without being paid, are called:

options.a: Brand advocates
options.b: Wholesalers
options.c: Paid influencers
options.d: Competitors

questions.explanation: Brand advocates are satisfied customers who freely promote the brand, and their recommendations are a major driver of positive word-of-mouth. Paid influencers (option C) are compensated, and wholesalers (option B) are channel members.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: A Nigerian payment app gives existing users N500 for every friend they get to sign up using their personal code. This programme is mainly a way of:

options.a: Organising personal selling by the sales force
options.b: Encouraging word-of-mouth through referral marketing
options.c: Issuing a press release
options.d: Running a television advertising campaign

questions.explanation: A referral programme rewards existing customers for recommending the product, which deliberately stimulates word-of-mouth. No TV adverts (option D), press release (option C) or sales force (option A) are involved.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: 'Organic reach' on social media refers to:

options.a: The number of people reached by paid adverts only
options.b: The number of farm products advertised online
options.c: The number of people who see a brand's content without the brand paying to promote it
options.d: The number of staff who manage the brand's pages

questions.explanation: Organic reach is free exposure from followers seeing and sharing a post, while paid reach comes from boosted posts or ads. Option A is paid reach, and option B takes 'organic' literally.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Many brands find that only a small share of their followers see their unpaid posts, because platforms decide what appears in users' feeds. As a result, brands often:

options.a: Stop creating content altogether
options.b: Pay to boost posts so they reach more people
options.c: Delete all their social media accounts
options.d: Rely only on the grapevine within the company

questions.explanation: Platform algorithms limit how many followers see unpaid posts, so brands combine organic content with paid promotion to extend reach. Options C and A would remove the brand from social media entirely, and the grapevine (option D) is internal to an organisation.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Content marketing is best described as:

options.a: Copying competitors' adverts word for word
options.b: Selling the content of a warehouse at a discount
options.c: Printing content on product packages only
options.d: Creating and sharing valuable, relevant content, such as articles, videos and tips, to attract and keep a target audience

questions.explanation: Content marketing attracts customers by giving them useful or entertaining content rather than direct sales messages, for example a bank sharing money-saving tips. Option A is unethical copying, and option B confuses 'content' with stock.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: In the internet era, consumers increasingly search for brand information, follow pages and choose what content to watch. This means marketing communication has moved more towards:

options.a: Communication without any channels
options.b: Communication only through door-to-door selling
options.c: Push communication only, where consumers cannot avoid messages
options.d: Pull communication, where consumers seek out the messages they want

questions.explanation: With search engines and social media, consumers pull information when they want it, so brands must create content people choose to find and follow. Option C describes interruptive mass advertising, which consumers can increasingly skip or block.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Which of the following features makes content most likely to go viral?

options.a: It is very long and full of technical details
options.b: It avoids any emotion and humour
options.c: It is shown only once to a small group
options.d: It is emotional, entertaining or useful enough that people want to share it

questions.explanation: People share content that makes them laugh, feel strongly or learn something useful, which is what drives viral spread. Long technical content (option A), very limited exposure (option C) and emotionless content (option B) give people little reason to pass it on.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: A key limitation of viral marketing is that:

options.a: It only works for government agencies
options.b: It always costs more than television advertising
options.c: Firms cannot guarantee that the content will spread or control how people interpret it
options.d: It cannot be used on the internet

questions.explanation: Whether content goes viral depends on consumers choosing to share it, so results are unpredictable and the message may be changed or criticised as it spreads. Viral campaigns are often cheap (option B), are mainly internet-based (option D), and are used by all kinds of organisations (option A).

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of internet-based marketing communication over traditional mass media?

options.a: Responses such as clicks, views and shares can be measured quickly and accurately
options.b: It never requires any creative ideas
options.c: It removes all competition among firms
options.d: It reaches only people without phones

questions.explanation: Online channels record actions such as clicks, views, shares and purchases, so firms can measure results and adjust campaigns quickly, which is harder with TV or print. Options B, D and C are untrue of internet communication.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a form of electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM)?

options.a: A tweet recommending a restaurant
options.b: A customer's product review on an online store
options.c: A company's television commercial
options.d: A forum post complaining about a phone brand

questions.explanation: eWOM is created by consumers and shared online, while a TV commercial is paid advertising created by the company. Options B, A and D are all consumer opinions shared over the internet.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Social media influencers are often seen as an online version of which traditional marketing communication concept?

options.a: Wholesalers
options.b: Opinion leaders
options.c: Market regulators
options.d: Retail sales assistants

questions.explanation: Opinion leaders are people whose advice and views influence others in their group, and influencers play this role online for their followers. Wholesalers (option A) are channel intermediaries, and retail sales assistants (option D) are employees doing personal selling.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: When a negative post about a company starts spreading on social media, the generally recommended response is to:

options.a: Argue aggressively with the customers in public
options.b: Ignore it completely and hope it disappears
options.c: Respond quickly, honestly and politely, and address the problem openly
options.d: Delete every critical comment and block the customers

questions.explanation: Fast, transparent and respectful responses show customers that the firm takes complaints seriously and can limit damage to reputation. Ignoring the issue (option B), deleting comments (option D) or arguing publicly (option A) usually makes the situation worse.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Interactivity, as a key feature of internet marketing communication, means:

options.a: Messages are sent only by firms and never answered
options.b: Firms and consumers can communicate with each other in both directions and respond to each other's messages
options.c: Communication takes place only through printed media
options.d: Consumers can watch adverts only at a fixed time

questions.explanation: Interactivity allows a two-way exchange: customers can comment, ask, rate and share, and brands can respond, often in real time. Option A describes one-way communication, and options D and C describe traditional media.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Platforms mainly used for sharing photos and videos, such as YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, are best classified as:

options.a: Media-sharing networks
options.b: Search engines
options.c: Online banking platforms
options.d: Professional networking sites

questions.explanation: Media-sharing networks are built around posting and viewing photos and videos, which makes them powerful for visual brand content. A professional networking site (option D) is built around careers and business contacts, as LinkedIn is, and search engines (option B) help users find information across the web.

questions.topic: MarCom in the Internet Era, Social Media and Word-of-Mouth
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a risk of using social media for marketing communication?

options.a: Negative comments spreading quickly to many people
options.b: Fake reviews misleading customers
options.c: Influencer scandals damaging the brand's image
options.d: Reaching large audiences at relatively low cost

questions.explanation: Reaching large audiences cheaply is one of the main benefits of social media, not a risk. Fast-spreading negative comments (option A), scandals involving influencers linked to the brand (option C) and fake reviews (option B) are all genuine risks firms must manage.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: The role of communication in market relationships is to:

options.a: Complete a single sale with no further contact
options.b: Minimise contact with customers to save resources
options.c: Build trust, loyalty and lasting customer commitment
options.d: Restrict product availability to create scarcity

questions.explanation: Communication keeps a firm connected to its customers after the first sale, building the trust and loyalty that turn one-off buyers into long-term customers. Option A describes a pure one-off transaction, which is the opposite of a relationship, and Options B and D would weaken the relationship.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: An interactional approach to communication focuses on:

options.a: One-way messages that the business fully controls
options.b: Suppressing feedback to maintain authority
options.c: Reducing advertising costs without strategy
options.d: Two-way dialogue between businesses and customers

questions.explanation: The interactional approach sees communication as an exchange in which both the business and the customer send and respond to messages. Option A is the opposite, a one-way or linear view of communication, and Options B and C have nothing to do with interaction.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A relational approach to communication is centred on:

options.a: Maximising the profit from each single transaction
options.b: Sending the same mass message to all audiences
options.c: Building lasting, value-based relationships with customers
options.d: Reducing contact with customers after a sale

questions.explanation: The relational approach treats communication as a way of creating and keeping long-term relationships that give value to both the customer and the firm. Option A is a transactional, one-off focus, Option B ignores the relationship context, and Option D would end the relationship instead of building it.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A network approach to communication emphasises:

options.a: Communication between one seller and one buyer only
options.b: One-way messages from the firm to the mass market
options.c: Communication limited to departments inside the firm
options.d: Connected exchanges among many stakeholders, including partners and suppliers

questions.explanation: The network approach looks beyond a single buyer and seller to the web of relationships among suppliers, distributors, partners, customers and others, all communicating with each other. Option A is a single dyad, Option B is mass one-way communication, and Option C is internal communication only.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Communication in market relationships strategically aims to:

options.a: Avoid customer engagement to streamline operations
options.b: Win a sale once and then end contact
options.c: Restrict product availability to increase demand
options.d: Strengthen customer loyalty through consistent delivery of value

questions.explanation: When a firm keeps communicating and keeps delivering what it promises, customers grow loyal and keep buying. Option B is a short-term, transactional view, Option A reduces the contact that relationships depend on, and Option C is a distribution tactic, not a communication aim.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: An interactional approach to communication ensures:

options.a: Feedback is suppressed so the firm keeps control
options.b: Active engagement with customers and responsiveness to their needs
options.c: Messages flow only from the firm to the customer
options.d: Customers receive messages but cannot reply

questions.explanation: Because the interactional approach is built on two-way exchange, the firm listens to customers and responds to what they say and need. Options A, C and D all describe one-way communication with no real customer input, which is the opposite of interaction.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A relational approach to communication enables businesses to:

options.a: Focus only on one-off sales
options.b: Build trust and develop long-term partnerships with customers
options.c: Minimise customer engagement to save resources
options.d: Constrain product availability to create exclusivity

questions.explanation: Relational communication keeps a steady, trusted connection with customers so the relationship grows into a long-term partnership. Option A is the transactional approach the relational view moves away from, and Options C and D would weaken rather than build relationships.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A network approach to communication is valuable for:

options.a: Dealing with one customer at a time in isolation
options.b: Keeping communication within a single department
options.c: Managing relationships across a web of interdependent stakeholders
options.d: Replacing all contact with suppliers and partners

questions.explanation: Businesses depend on many connected parties such as suppliers, distributors, partners and customers, and the network approach helps coordinate communication across all of them. Options A and B focus on a single relationship or unit, and Option D is the opposite of a network view.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Communication in market relationships fundamentally seeks to:

options.a: Avoid customer engagement to reduce costs
options.b: Attract new customers while ignoring existing ones
options.c: Increase customer trust, satisfaction and retention
options.d: Restrict product availability to build demand

questions.explanation: The purpose of relationship-focused communication is to keep customers satisfied and trusting so that they stay with the firm. Option B ignores retention, which is the heart of relationship marketing, Option A removes the contact relationships need, and Option D is a distribution tactic.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A relational approach to communication treats which of the following as a basis of competitive advantage?

options.a: The lowest possible price on each single transaction
options.b: The largest possible number of one-off buyers
options.c: The cheapest possible advertising medium
options.d: Sustained, long-term customer relationships

questions.explanation: Under the relational approach, loyal long-term customers are hard for competitors to copy or steal, so the relationship itself becomes an advantage. Options A and B focus on single transactions rather than relationships, and Option C is a media cost choice.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A network approach to communication supports businesses by:

options.a: Limiting communication to the firm and its final customers
options.b: Removing the need to communicate with suppliers
options.c: Enabling effective collaboration across different stakeholder groups
options.d: Making each department communicate only internally

questions.explanation: Since the network approach links many stakeholders, it helps a business coordinate and collaborate with suppliers, distributors, partners and customers together. Option A leaves out the wider network, Option B contradicts it, and Option D keeps communication inside the firm.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Of the different types of exchange, which two can be most readily observed in marketing, with marketing communications playing roles in both?

options.a: Barter exchange and monetary exchange
options.b: Market exchange and relational exchange
options.c: Direct exchange and indirect exchange
options.d: Internal exchange and external exchange

questions.explanation: Market (transactional) exchanges and relational exchanges are the two types of exchange most easily observed, and marketing communications supports both of them. Options A, C and D are other ways of grouping transactions, but they are not the pair used to explain the role of communication in market relationships.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: The shift away from reliance on one-off market exchanges towards a longer-term perspective that creates and maintains enduring partnerships with customers is known as:

options.a: Relationship marketing
options.b: Transactional marketing
options.c: Mass marketing
options.d: Production orientation

questions.explanation: Relationship marketing is the long-term approach that focuses on creating and keeping lasting partnerships with customers instead of chasing single sales. Option B, transactional marketing, is exactly the one-off market exchange approach the shift moves away from, while options C and D focus on reaching everyone or on making products efficiently.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A market (transactional) exchange is best described as:

options.a: A one-off, short-term exchange focused mainly on the product and its price
options.b: An exchange between departments inside the same organisation
options.c: An exchange in which buyer and seller jointly plan future products together
options.d: A long-term exchange built on trust and repeated contact over many years

questions.explanation: A market or transactional exchange is a discrete, short-term deal in which the focus is on completing the sale, usually on the basis of product and price. Options C and D describe relational exchange, where parties stay connected and cooperate over time, and option B is internal communication, not a market exchange.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A relational exchange is best described as:

options.a: An exchange carried out only through mass media advertising
options.b: An ongoing exchange in which buyer and seller build trust and interact repeatedly over time
options.c: An exchange in which price is the only thing both parties care about
options.d: A single exchange that ends once the goods and payment have changed hands

questions.explanation: Relational exchange is long-term: buyer and seller keep dealing with each other, develop trust and commitment, and see value in continuing the relationship. Options C and D describe a one-off market exchange, and option A wrongly ties relational exchange to a single one-way channel.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Chidi buys a used phone charger from a hawker at a Lagos bus stop. They bargain over the price, he pays N2,500, and neither expects to deal with the other again. This is an example of:

options.a: A long-term relational exchange
options.b: A network-based exchange
options.c: A strategic business partnership
options.d: A market (transactional) exchange

questions.explanation: This is a market or transactional exchange because it is a single deal, the focus is on price, and there is no expectation of future dealings. Option A would require repeated contact and a developing relationship, and options B and C involve ongoing links between several parties or organisations.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A cement manufacturer and a construction company in Abuja have dealt with each other for eight years. They share delivery schedules, plan supply together for new projects, and resolve problems through regular meetings. Their exchange is best described as:

options.a: A market (transactional) exchange
options.b: A relational exchange
options.c: A barter exchange
options.d: A one-off spot purchase

questions.explanation: Long-term dealings, information sharing and joint planning are signs of a relational exchange, in which both parties value keeping the relationship going. Options A and D describe single, short-term deals, and option C is about swapping goods without money, which is not what is happening here.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: In a purely transactional (market) exchange, the main role of marketing communication is usually to:

options.a: Inform and persuade buyers about the offer so that a sale is completed
options.b: Develop deep trust and commitment over many years of dialogue
options.c: Coordinate joint planning between long-term partner organisations
options.d: Maintain an ongoing personal relationship after every purchase

questions.explanation: In a one-off market exchange, communication mainly informs buyers about the product and price and persuades them to buy now. Options B, C and D describe what communication does in relational exchanges, where the goal is to keep and deepen a relationship over time.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: In a relational exchange, the main role of marketing communication is to:

options.a: Replace all personal contact with one-way mass advertising
options.b: Close a single sale as quickly as possible at the best price
options.c: Build and maintain trust, commitment and dialogue between the parties
options.d: Announce product features once and then stop all contact

questions.explanation: When an exchange is relational, communication is used to keep the relationship alive: it builds trust and commitment and keeps a two-way dialogue going. Option B is the aim of a one-off transactional exchange, while options A and D cut off the ongoing contact that relationships depend on.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Relationship marketing is best defined as:

options.a: Reducing prices below competitors to win one-off sales
options.b: Attracting, maintaining and enhancing long-term relationships with customers
options.c: Selling as many units as possible to new customers in one season
options.d: Communicating with customers only through mass advertising

questions.explanation: Relationship marketing focuses on attracting customers and then keeping and strengthening relationships with them over the long term. Options A and C are short-term, sale-by-sale approaches, and option D is one-way mass communication rather than relationship building.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Which statement best captures the idea behind relationship marketing?

options.a: Marketing ends the moment the customer has paid, so no further contact is needed
options.b: Marketing is mainly about producing goods as cheaply and efficiently as possible
options.c: Marketing is only about advertising on television and radio to reach many people
options.d: Marketing is not just about selling products; it is about building relationships and creating value

questions.explanation: Relationship marketing sees marketing as building lasting relationships and creating value for both sides, not just making a sale. Option A reflects a one-off transactional view, option B is a production view, and option C confuses marketing with a single promotional tool.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: In relationship marketing, a customer's confidence in a supplier's reliability and integrity is called:

options.a: Commitment
options.b: Satisfaction
options.c: Trust
options.d: Awareness

questions.explanation: Trust is the confidence one party has that the other is reliable, honest and will keep its promises. Option A, commitment, is the desire to keep a valued relationship going, while options B and D are about knowing a brand exists and being pleased with a purchase.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: An enduring desire by a customer to maintain a valued relationship with a firm is called:

options.a: Commitment
options.b: Brand awareness
options.c: Trial
options.d: Trust

questions.explanation: Commitment is the lasting wish to keep a relationship going because it is valued. Option D, trust, is confidence in the partner's reliability, which helps create commitment but is not the same thing; options B and C are early stages of buyer behaviour.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Which two variables are regarded as central to the success of relationship marketing?

options.a: Price and discounts
options.b: Speed and volume
options.c: Awareness and reach
options.d: Trust and commitment

questions.explanation: Trust and commitment are treated as the key ingredients of successful long-term relationships: when they are present, partners cooperate and stay together. Options A, B and C matter in marketing generally but they do not hold a relationship together over time.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: For five years, a Kano wholesaler has always delivered rice to a retailer on the agreed date, in the agreed quantity and at the agreed price. The retailer now places orders without checking every bag. The quality the retailer has developed towards the wholesaler is best described as:

options.a: Trust
options.b: Impulse buying
options.c: Cognitive dissonance
options.d: Brand switching

questions.explanation: The retailer has developed trust: years of reliable, honest delivery give confidence that the wholesaler will keep its promises. Option D means moving to a competitor, option C is post-purchase doubt, and option B is unplanned buying, none of which fit the case.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Aisha has banked with the same bank for ten years. Another bank offers her a slightly better savings rate, but she stays because she values her relationship with her account officer and the bank. Her behaviour mainly shows:

options.a: Price sensitivity
options.b: Commitment to the relationship
options.c: A transactional orientation
options.d: Brand switching

questions.explanation: Aisha stays even when a rival offers a better deal because she values the relationship, which is what commitment means. Options A and D would lead her to move for the better rate, and option C describes someone who judges each deal only on its own terms.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Customer retention refers to:

options.a: The number of new products a firm launches each year
options.b: The amount a firm spends on television advertising
options.c: A firm's ability to keep its existing customers buying from it over time
options.d: A firm's ability to attract first-time buyers from rival brands

questions.explanation: Customer retention is about keeping current customers coming back over time. Option D describes customer acquisition and brand switching, while options A and B are measures of product development and media spending.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Relationship marketing places strong emphasis on customer retention mainly because:

options.a: Existing customers never compare prices with competitors
options.b: New customers always spend more than existing customers
options.c: Retention removes the need for any marketing communication
options.d: Keeping an existing customer usually costs less than attracting a new one

questions.explanation: It generally costs less to keep a customer than to win a new one, and loyal customers tend to buy more and recommend the firm, so retention is profitable. Option B is untrue as a general rule, option A is unrealistic, and option C is wrong because retention itself depends on continued communication.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of relational exchange?

options.a: Long-term orientation towards keeping the customer
options.b: Trust and commitment between buyer and seller
options.c: Regular two-way communication and feedback over time
options.d: Focus on completing a single sale with no further contact

questions.explanation: A focus on a single sale with no further contact is the mark of a transactional exchange, not a relational one. Options A, B and C are all typical features of relational exchange, which is long-term, trust-based and kept alive by ongoing dialogue.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typical of a transactional approach to marketing?

options.a: A short time scale for each exchange
options.b: High emphasis on customer service and long-term contact
options.c: Emphasis on product features and on price
options.d: Focus on completing each single sale on its own

questions.explanation: A strong emphasis on customer service and continuing contact belongs to relationship marketing. Options A, C and D are classic features of transactional marketing, which looks at each sale on its own, stresses features and price, and has a short time horizon.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Compared with transactional marketing, relationship marketing focuses more on:

options.a: Customer value and benefits over a long time scale
options.b: Mass production at the lowest possible cost
options.c: Single sales with limited customer contact
options.d: Product features over a short time scale

questions.explanation: Relationship marketing centres on the value the customer gets over time and on keeping the customer. Options C and D describe the transactional approach, and option B is a production orientation rather than either marketing approach.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Customer lifetime value is best described as:

options.a: The price a customer pays for the firm's most expensive single product
options.b: The value of the very first purchase a customer makes with the firm
options.c: The number of years a product stays on the market before withdrawal
options.d: The total value a customer is expected to bring to a firm over the whole relationship

questions.explanation: Customer lifetime value looks at the whole stream of purchases a customer is expected to make over the entire relationship, which is why it supports retention. Option B looks only at one sale, option A at one price, and option C at the product life cycle rather than the customer.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A supermarket in Ikeja gives shoppers a card that earns points on every purchase, which can later be redeemed for gifts. The main relationship marketing purpose of this card is to:

options.a: Attract only one-time buyers from other cities
options.b: Reduce the number of visits each customer makes
options.c: Encourage repeat purchases and retain customers
options.d: Replace the need to stock popular products

questions.explanation: A points card rewards customers each time they come back, so its main aim is repeat buying and customer retention. Option A targets one-off buyers, option B is the opposite of what the card aims for, and option D has nothing to do with loyalty schemes.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: On the relationship marketing 'ladder of loyalty', a customer who actively recommends the firm to other people is described as:

options.a: A lapsed customer
options.b: An advocate
options.c: A prospect
options.d: A first-time customer

questions.explanation: An advocate is a customer who has moved high up the loyalty ladder and actively speaks well of the firm to others. Option C has not yet bought, option D has bought only once, and option A has stopped buying.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: The rate at which customers stop doing business with a firm over a period is known as:

options.a: Customer churn (defection)
options.b: Customer acquisition
options.c: Market penetration
options.d: Brand awareness

questions.explanation: Churn, or defection, measures how many customers a firm loses over a period, so lowering it is a key goal of relationship marketing. Option B is gaining new customers, option C is selling more in existing markets, and option D is how well people know the brand.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: The interactional approach to communication views communication as:

options.a: A process whose meaning depends only on the medium through which it is sent
options.b: A message passed only through mass media with no response from the audience
options.c: A two-way process in which participants send messages, respond and give feedback to each other
options.d: A one-way flow of messages from a sender to a passive receiver who does not reply

questions.explanation: In the interactional approach, communication is an interaction: both parties send and receive messages and respond to each other through feedback. Options B and D describe a one-way linear view, and option A wrongly makes the medium the only thing that matters.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: The interactional approach to communication differs from the simple linear model mainly because it:

options.a: Removes the receiver from the communication process
options.b: Treats the sender as the only active participant
options.c: Assumes every message is understood exactly as intended
options.d: Includes feedback and response, so communication flows both ways

questions.explanation: The linear model shows messages moving one way from sender to receiver, whereas the interactional approach adds response and feedback so that both sides take part. Options B and C are features of the linear view, and option A would mean there is no communication at all.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A customer complains on social media that her mobile data was wrongly deducted. The telecom firm replies within minutes, asks for details, she responds, and the firm fixes the problem and checks back with her. This exchange best illustrates the:

options.a: Linear (one-way) model of communication
options.b: Network approach to communication
options.c: Interactional approach to communication
options.d: Mass broadcast approach

questions.explanation: Both parties keep sending messages and responding to each other, which is the two-way exchange at the heart of the interactional approach. Options A and D involve one-way messages with no response, and option B is about messages spreading across a wide web of many people.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Which element is most central to the interactional approach to communication?

options.a: The number of people reached by one message
options.b: Feedback and response between the parties
options.c: The colour and design of the advertisement
options.d: The size of the media budget

questions.explanation: The interactional approach depends on the parties responding to each other, so feedback is its core element. Options A, C and D concern spending, reach and creative design, which matter in campaigns but do not define interaction.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Communication in which both parties listen, respond and build shared understanding together, rather than one party simply talking at the other, is best described as:

options.a: Dialogue
options.b: Propaganda
options.c: Broadcasting
options.d: Monologue

questions.explanation: Dialogue is a two-way conversation where both sides listen and respond, and it is what interactional and relationship-based communication aim for. Options C and D are one-way forms of communication, and option B is one-sided persuasion that does not invite a reply.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: The relational (contextual) approach to communication holds that:

options.a: Only the technical quality of the channel decides how a message is understood
options.b: Communication works best when the parties have no previous relationship at all
options.c: The meaning of a message is fixed and identical for every receiver in every situation
options.d: Meaning depends on the relationship between the participants and the context of the message

questions.explanation: The relational or contextual approach says that people interpret messages through the relationship they have with each other and the situation they are in. Option C ignores context, option A looks only at the channel, and option B contradicts the idea that relationships shape communication.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Two suppliers send a food processor in Ibadan the same message: 'Your order will arrive tomorrow.' The processor fully believes the supplier it has used reliably for years but doubts the new supplier. This difference is best explained by the:

options.a: Relational (contextual) approach to communication
options.b: Linear (one-way) model of communication
options.c: Hypodermic needle view of communication
options.d: Mass media approach

questions.explanation: The same words are interpreted differently because of the relationship and history between the parties, which is the central idea of the relational or contextual approach. Options B, C and D all assume a message has the same effect regardless of who sends it or the relationship involved.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Which pairing correctly matches each approach to communication with its main focus?

options.a: Interactional - meaning shaped by context; relational - one-way flow of messages
options.b: Interactional - one-way flow of messages; relational - spread across many people
options.c: Interactional - two-way message exchange; relational - meaning shaped by the relationship
options.d: Interactional - spread across many people; relational - one-way flow of messages

questions.explanation: The interactional approach stresses the two-way exchange of messages with response and feedback, while the relational or contextual approach stresses that the relationship and context give messages their meaning. Options A, B and D mix these up or attach the linear and network ideas to the wrong approach.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: The relational approach to communication is mainly concerned with:

options.a: Communication that develops and sustains the relationship between the parties
options.b: Communication that persuades a buyer to make one quick purchase
options.c: Communication that depends only on the price of the product
options.d: Communication that avoids any reply from the receiver

questions.explanation: The relational approach focuses on how communication builds and keeps up the relationship between the parties, which in turn shapes how later messages are understood. Option B is a transactional aim, option D is one-way communication, and option C ignores the relationship altogether.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: The network approach to communication views communication as:

options.a: Flows of information through a web of interconnected people and organisations
options.b: A process that takes place only inside one department
options.c: A private exchange that never spreads beyond two people
options.d: A single message passing from one sender to one receiver only

questions.explanation: The network approach sees communication as moving through networks: many linked individuals and organisations pass information to each other. Options B, C and D all restrict communication to a single link or a closed group, which is the opposite of a network view.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: News about a new fintech app spreads among UNILAG students: a few share it in their class WhatsApp groups, members forward it to other groups, and within days thousands have heard about it. This pattern is best explained by the:

options.a: Relational (contextual) approach to communication
options.b: Network approach to communication
options.c: Linear (one-way) model of communication
options.d: Personal selling process

questions.explanation: The message is moving from person to person across many linked groups, which is exactly what the network approach describes. Option C is a single one-way flow, option A focuses on how one relationship shapes meaning, and option D is a salesperson dealing directly with a buyer.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Which approach to communication best explains how word-of-mouth and viral messages spread among consumers?

options.a: The linear approach
options.b: The interactional approach between two parties only
options.c: The production approach
options.d: The network approach

questions.explanation: Word of mouth and viral messages travel from person to person through webs of contacts, which is what the network approach explains. Option A is one-way communication, option B is limited to two parties, and option C is a business orientation, not a communication approach.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: In the network approach, people who are well connected and pass information on to many others are important because they:

options.a: Remove the need for any message to be sent at all
options.b: Stop messages from reaching other members of the network
options.c: Speed up and widen the spread of messages through the network
options.d: Only receive messages and never share them with others

questions.explanation: Well-connected members, such as opinion leaders, act as hubs that carry messages to many other people, so they speed up and widen diffusion. Options B and D describe people who block or absorb information, and option A makes no sense because a network still needs messages.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A beverage company in Lagos coordinates its communication with suppliers, distributors, retailers, advertising agencies and regulators, recognising that information passes among all of them. This view is best described as the:

options.a: Network approach to communication
options.b: Hypodermic needle view of communication
options.c: Transactional approach to exchange
options.d: Linear approach to communication

questions.explanation: Seeing communication as flowing among many interconnected organisations in and around the distribution channel is the network approach. Options B and D treat communication as one-way from one sender, and option C is about one-off exchanges rather than how communication flows.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: The interactional, relational (contextual) and network approaches all differ from the simple linear model of communication in that they:

options.a: Focus only on the technical channel used to carry the message
options.b: Ignore feedback and response between the sender and the receiver
options.c: Treat communication as more than a one-way transmission from sender to receiver
options.d: Assume the receiver is passive and never responds to any message

questions.explanation: All three approaches move beyond the idea of a one-way message: they add response, relationships, context and networks of people. Options A, B and D are actually limitations of the linear view that these approaches set out to correct.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit a firm usually gains from strong customer relationships?

options.a: Customers who are less likely to switch to rivals
options.b: Positive word-of-mouth recommendations
options.c: Customers who buy once and never return
options.d: More repeat purchases

questions.explanation: Customers who buy once and disappear are what poor relationships produce, so this is not a benefit. Options A, B and D are all typical rewards of good relationships: loyal customers buy again, recommend the firm and resist rival offers.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A Nigerian telecom operator sends each subscriber a personalised birthday message with bonus airtime, and its customer care team remembers past complaints when customers call. These actions are best described as:

options.a: Price skimming
options.b: Mass marketing
options.c: Transactional marketing
options.d: Relationship marketing

questions.explanation: Personalised recognition and remembering each customer's history are ways of building long-term relationships and loyalty. Option C focuses on single sales, option B treats all customers the same, and option A is a pricing strategy for new products.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Customer loyalty is best described as:

options.a: A customer's first trial purchase of a newly launched brand
options.b: A customer's formal complaint to the firm about a faulty product
options.c: A customer's continued preference for and repeat purchase of a firm's brand over time
options.d: A customer's habit of always switching to whichever brand is cheapest

questions.explanation: Loyalty means the customer keeps preferring and buying the same brand over time, which is a main goal of relationship marketing. Option A is trial, option D is price-driven switching, and option B is a service recovery situation.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: In a transactional exchange, the relationship between buyer and seller typically:

options.a: Requires regular two-way meetings to sustain it
options.b: Ends once the goods and payment have been exchanged
options.c: Depends heavily on trust built over repeated dealings
options.d: Continues for many years through joint planning

questions.explanation: A transactional exchange is complete once the product and payment change hands; nothing binds the parties to continue. Options A, C and D describe the continuing, trust-based contact of relational exchange.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: A relational exchange is characterised by interdependence, which means that:

options.a: Each party acts alone and ignores the other's interests
options.b: Each party relies on the other and gains from continuing the relationship
options.c: The parties never communicate after the first sale
options.d: Only the seller benefits from the exchange

questions.explanation: Interdependence means both sides depend on each other and benefit from keeping the relationship going, so they cooperate. Option A describes independent, one-off dealing, option D is one-sided, and option C describes a transactional exchange.

questions.topic: Communication in Market Relationships
questions.question: Among the conditions for exchange, the requirement that 'each party trusts and respects the other sufficiently to take the exchange seriously' shows that even a single transaction depends on:

options.a: The use of television advertising
options.b: The seller offering the lowest price in the market
options.c: A long-term written contract
options.d: A basic level of trust between the parties

questions.explanation: Even a one-off exchange needs enough trust for both parties to take it seriously, which is why trust is so central when exchanges become long-term relationships. Option C is not required for every exchange, and options A and B are marketing choices, not conditions of exchange.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Online communication media are best exemplified by:

options.a: Traditional broadcast channels like television and radio
options.b: Print publications like newspapers and magazines
options.c: Outdoor advertising like billboards and posters
options.d: Digital platforms such as social media, websites and apps

questions.explanation: Online media are channels that work over the internet, such as social media, websites, mobile apps and email. Options A, B and C are all offline or traditional media, because they reach audiences through broadcast signals, paper or physical sites.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Offline communication media are characterised by:

options.a: Digital channels like email and social media
options.b: Online platforms like websites and blogs
options.c: Traditional outlets such as television, radio and print advertising
options.d: Streaming services and podcasts

questions.explanation: Offline media are the traditional, non-internet channels such as television, radio, newspapers, magazines and billboards. Options A, B and D all depend on the internet, so they are online media.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Crafting digital marketing involves:

options.a: Copying a print advert unchanged onto every website
options.b: Avoiding any measurement of online results
options.c: Developing strategic content suited to how audiences behave online
options.d: Ignoring which platforms the target audience uses

questions.explanation: Good digital marketing starts from how the target audience searches, browses and interacts online, and then plans content and channels to match. Option A ignores the differences between platforms, Option B throws away one of digital marketing's biggest strengths, and Option D would waste the budget on the wrong channels.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Digital marketing communication includes:

options.a: Targeted email campaigns and social media advertising
options.b: Traditional television and radio commercials
options.c: Print media like newspapers and magazines
options.d: Physical signage like billboards and flyers

questions.explanation: Email campaigns and social media adverts are digital because they are delivered over the internet and can be aimed at specific people. Options B, C and D are traditional offline media.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is a form of digital marketing?

options.a: Direct mail campaigns targeting local markets
options.b: Search engine optimisation (SEO) to improve online visibility
options.c: Television advertising for mass reach
options.d: Print advertising in trade journals

questions.explanation: SEO means improving a website so that it ranks higher in search engine results, making it easier for people to find online. Option A is posted letters or leaflets, Option C is broadcast media, and Option D is print media, so none of them is digital.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: The strategic importance of digital marketing lies in its ability to:

options.a: Reach only customers within walking distance of a shop
options.b: Reach large and even global audiences efficiently and at relatively low cost
options.c: Remove the need for any marketing plan
options.d: Work only for very large companies

questions.explanation: Digital channels let even a small firm reach audiences far beyond its location, often for less money than traditional media, and campaigns can be scaled up or down easily. Option A describes a very local reach, Option C is wrong because digital marketing still needs planning, and Option D ignores its use by small businesses.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Online communication media stand out because of their capacity to:

options.a: Deliver only one-way messages with no response
options.b: Reach audiences without any need for the internet
options.c: Deliver precise, interactive and data-driven interaction with audiences
options.d: Avoid collecting any data on audience behaviour

questions.explanation: Online media let firms aim messages at specific people, let those people respond, and record data on how they react. Option A describes traditional one-way media, Option B contradicts what 'online' means, and Option D ignores the data these channels produce.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Offline communication media remain relevant because they:

options.a: Offer more precise tracking of results than online media
options.b: Allow instant two-way chat with every viewer
options.c: Depend completely on internet access
options.d: Reach audiences, including local ones, through established traditional channels

questions.explanation: Traditional media such as radio, newspapers and billboards still reach many people, including those who use the internet less, and local radio or posters are good for reaching a particular community. Option A is wrong because online media are easier to track, Option B describes online interaction, and Option C contradicts the meaning of offline.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Crafting effective digital marketing requires:

options.a: Using exactly the same message on every platform
options.b: Suppressing feedback to maintain authority
options.c: Focusing only on the lowest-cost channel
options.d: Deep insight into online consumer behaviour and how each platform works

questions.explanation: To succeed online, marketers need to understand how their audience behaves online and what works on each platform, since a format that works on one may fail on another. Option A ignores platform differences, Option B throws away valuable feedback, and Option C chooses channels on cost instead of audience fit.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Digital marketing communication enables businesses to:

options.a: Monitor and analyse campaign performance with real-time metrics
options.b: Avoid measuring campaign results
options.c: Wait until the end of the year to see any results
options.d: Reach customers only through printed materials

questions.explanation: Digital tools record clicks, views, shares and sales as they happen, so firms can see at once how a campaign is doing and adjust it. Option B and Option C ignore this real-time tracking, and Option D describes offline print media.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is a type of digital marketing?

options.a: Television commercials for broad awareness
options.b: Newspaper adverts for regional reach
options.c: Pay-per-click (PPC) advertising for immediate website traffic
options.d: Direct mail for personalised outreach

questions.explanation: In pay-per-click advertising, an advertiser pays each time someone clicks its online ad, which can bring visitors to a website quickly. Options A, B and D are broadcast, print and postal media, which are traditional offline channels.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: The value of digital marketing is shown by its ability to:

options.a: Prevent customers from giving feedback
options.b: Slow down communication with customers
options.c: Allow instant customer engagement and quick responses
options.d: Limit a firm to a single message for all customers

questions.explanation: Digital channels let customers comment, ask and share immediately, and let firms respond within minutes, keeping conversations alive. Option A and Option B are the opposite of what digital marketing offers, and Option D ignores its ability to tailor messages.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Online communication media include:

options.a: Traditional television and radio broadcasts
options.b: Print media like newspapers and magazines
options.c: Email marketing and online display advertisements
options.d: Outdoor signage like billboards and flyers

questions.explanation: Email marketing and online display ads are delivered through the internet, so they are online media. Options A, B and D are offline media that reach people through broadcast signals, paper or physical locations.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Offline communication media are effective for:

options.a: Tracking each viewer's clicks in real time
options.b: Strengthening brand presence through tangible, traditional touchpoints
options.c: Targeting individuals by their online browsing data
options.d: Allowing instant replies in comment threads

questions.explanation: Physical and traditional media such as billboards, print adverts, flyers and broadcast commercials keep a brand visible in people's everyday surroundings. Options A, C and D describe strengths of online media, which rely on internet data and interaction.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Digital marketing communication is distinguished by its:

options.a: One-way flow and difficulty of measurement
options.b: Dependence on printed materials
options.c: Interactivity, measurability and adaptability to audience needs
options.d: Fixed messages that cannot be changed once launched

questions.explanation: Digital communication lets audiences respond, records detailed results and can be changed quickly to suit different audiences. Option A describes traditional media, Option B is offline print, and Option D is wrong because digital campaigns can be edited quickly.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: An important benefit of digital marketing is its capacity to:

options.a: Avoid customer interaction to reduce costs
options.b: Send identical messages to all customers
options.c: Remove the need to understand customer needs
options.d: Improve customer experiences through personalisation and engagement

questions.explanation: Because digital channels collect data on customers, firms can tailor content and offers to each person and interact with them, making the experience more relevant. Option B ignores personalisation, Option A is the opposite of engagement, and Option C is wrong because personalisation depends on understanding customer needs.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is a group made up entirely of offline (traditional) media?

options.a: Television, radio, newspapers and billboards
options.b: Radio, social media, magazines and websites
options.c: Television, email, billboards and search engines
options.d: Websites, search engines, email and mobile apps

questions.explanation: Offline or traditional media are channels that do not need the internet, such as TV, radio, print and outdoor. Option D lists only online media, and options B and C mix offline channels with online ones such as email, search, social media and websites.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is a group made up entirely of online media?

options.a: Billboards, websites, radio and email
options.b: Newspapers, magazines, radio and television
options.c: Websites, search engines, social media and email
options.d: Television, social media, flyers and search engines

questions.explanation: Online media are internet-based channels such as websites, search engines, social media and email. Option B lists traditional offline media, while options A and D mix in billboards, radio, TV and flyers, which are offline.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an offline communication medium?

options.a: A sponsored search engine advertisement
options.b: A full-page newspaper advertisement
options.c: A radio jingle on a local station
options.d: A roadside billboard on a highway
