questions.explanation: A sponsored search ad appears on a search engine results page, so it is an online medium. Options B, C and D are outdoor, broadcast and print media, all of which are traditional offline channels.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an online communication medium?

options.a: A company's Instagram page
options.b: A painted advertisement on the side of a danfo bus
options.c: A banner advertisement on a news website
options.d: An email newsletter

questions.explanation: An advert painted on a bus is transit (outdoor) advertising, which is offline. Options A, C and D are social media, email and website display advertising, all delivered over the internet.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A major advantage of online media over most offline media is that online media:

options.a: Cannot be ignored, blocked or skipped by the audience
options.b: Always cost more than a national television campaign
options.c: Allow results such as clicks and views to be measured quickly
options.d: Reach people who have no internet access at all

questions.explanation: Online media make it easy to track how many people saw, clicked or bought, often in real time. Option D is actually a strength of offline media, option A is untrue because online ads are easily skipped, and option B is false since digital campaigns are often cheaper.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Compared with traditional offline media, online media are generally more:

options.a: Limited to local audiences only
options.b: Difficult to target at specific groups
options.c: One-way, giving the audience no chance to respond
options.d: Interactive, allowing two-way communication with the audience

questions.explanation: Online media let audiences reply, comment, share and click, so communication can flow both ways. Option C describes traditional broadcast media, and options A and B are the reverse of the truth, because online media can reach global audiences and target specific groups precisely.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: An agro-chemical firm wants to reach farmers in remote villages in Benue State where internet access is poor but most households listen to local-language programmes. The most suitable medium is:

options.a: Email marketing
options.b: Local radio
options.c: Instagram influencer posts
options.d: Search engine advertising

questions.explanation: Radio reaches people without internet, is cheap, can be in local languages and is widely listened to in rural areas. Options A, C and D all depend on internet access, which these farmers largely lack.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the main strength of television as an advertising medium?

options.a: It combines sight, sound and motion to reach a large mass audience
options.b: It reaches only a small, highly selective audience
options.c: It is the cheapest medium for very small local businesses
options.d: It allows readers to keep and re-read detailed information

questions.explanation: Television's power comes from combining pictures, sound and movement and from reaching very large audiences at once, although it is expensive. Option C is wrong because TV is costly, option D describes print, and option B is the opposite of TV's mass reach.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which offline medium is best known for being low cost, locally targeted and audio only?

options.a: Billboards
options.b: Radio
options.c: Magazines
options.d: Television

questions.explanation: Radio is relatively cheap, can be aimed at local listeners, and works through sound alone. Option D adds pictures and costs more, option C is a visual print medium, and option A is outdoor and visual.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which offline medium usually offers a long life, high-quality colour reproduction and a selective readership with specific interests?

options.a: Billboards
options.b: Radio
options.c: Newspapers
options.d: Magazines

questions.explanation: Magazines are kept and passed around for weeks, print in good colour and target readers with particular interests. Option C has a short life and lower print quality, option B has no visuals, and option A carries only brief messages to passers-by.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Compared with magazines, newspapers as an advertising medium are best known for:

options.a: Timeliness and local coverage, but a short life
options.b: Sound and motion to grab attention
options.c: A long life and highly selective readership
options.d: Personal two-way interaction with each reader

questions.explanation: Newspapers come out daily, so ads can be placed quickly and aimed at a city or region, but each edition is soon thrown away. Option C describes magazines, option B describes TV, and option D describes personal or interactive media.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Outdoor advertising such as billboards is best described as a medium that:

options.a: Gives repeated exposure to passers-by but carries only brief messages
options.b: Lets each viewer reply to the advertiser instantly
options.c: Allows long, detailed explanations of complex products
options.d: Reaches only people who subscribe to it

questions.explanation: Billboards are seen again and again by people passing the same spot, but they can only show a short message because people see them for a few seconds. Option C describes print, option B describes interactive online media, and option D describes email lists or magazine subscriptions.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A fashion brand in Lagos puts a QR code on its billboards on Third Mainland Bridge which takes viewers straight to its online store. This is an example of:

options.a: Using only offline media
options.b: Abandoning traditional advertising
options.c: Integrating offline and online media
options.d: Using only online media

questions.explanation: The billboard is offline and the online store is digital; linking them with a QR code integrates the two so they support each other. Options A and D each ignore one side of the campaign, and option B is wrong because the billboard is still being used.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of online media?

options.a: Messages may not reach people without internet access
options.b: Audiences can block or skip adverts
options.c: Heavy clutter from many competing messages
options.d: Results of campaigns can be tracked in detail

questions.explanation: Detailed tracking of results is one of the main advantages of online media, not a limitation. Options A, B and C are real drawbacks: limited internet access, ad blocking and skipping, and clutter.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Digital marketing is best defined as:

options.a: Printing brochures and handing them out to people on the street
options.b: Selling goods face to face to customers in physical markets and shops
options.c: The use of the internet and digital channels to promote products and engage customers
options.d: The use of only television and radio to advertise products to the public

questions.explanation: Digital marketing uses digital channels such as websites, search engines, social media, email and mobile to promote products and connect with customers. Option D is broadcast advertising, option B is personal selling, and option A is offline print promotion.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Promoting products and building customer relationships through websites, search engines, social media, email and mobile devices is called:

options.a: Outdoor advertising
options.b: Personal selling
options.c: Digital marketing
options.d: Trade promotion

questions.explanation: Using internet-based and mobile channels to promote and engage is digital marketing. Option A uses billboards and transit, option B is face-to-face selling, and option D targets intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical step in crafting a digital marketing strategy?

options.a: Setting clear objectives for the campaign
options.b: Choosing the right digital channels and content
options.c: Defining the target audience
options.d: Skipping measurement because digital results cannot be tracked

questions.explanation: Measuring results is a key step in digital marketing, and digital results can in fact be tracked closely, so skipping measurement is not part of a sound strategy. Options A, B and C are standard steps: set objectives, know the audience, and pick channels and content.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: When crafting digital marketing, using analytics after a campaign is launched mainly helps a firm to:

options.a: Stop customers from seeing competitors' ads
options.b: Remove the need to understand the target audience
options.c: Avoid setting any objectives for the campaign
options.d: Measure performance and improve the campaign based on the results

questions.explanation: Analytics show what is working, such as visits, clicks and sales, so the firm can adjust and optimise its campaign. Options B and C remove essential planning steps, and option A is not something analytics can do.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: In crafting digital marketing, a 'buyer persona' is:

options.a: A detailed profile representing a typical member of the target audience
options.b: A list of all the products a firm currently sells
options.c: The legal owner who registered the company's website
options.d: The password used to access the firm's social media page

questions.explanation: A buyer persona is a semi-fictional picture of a typical target customer, describing their needs, habits and online behaviour, which guides content and channel choices. Options B, C and D have nothing to do with understanding the audience.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Search engine optimisation (SEO) is best described as:

options.a: Paying the search engine each time someone clicks an advert
options.b: Sending promotional messages to a list of email subscribers
options.c: Improving a website so it ranks higher in unpaid (organic) search results
options.d: Paying celebrities to post about a product on their pages

questions.explanation: SEO improves a website's content, keywords and structure so that it appears higher in the free, organic search listings. Option A is pay-per-click advertising, option B is email marketing, and option D is influencer marketing.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A digital marketing method in which the advertiser pays a fee each time someone clicks on its advertisement is called:

options.a: Affiliate marketing
options.b: Search engine optimisation (SEO)
options.c: Content marketing
options.d: Pay-per-click (PPC) advertising

questions.explanation: In pay-per-click advertising the advertiser is charged only when someone clicks the ad, commonly on search engines. Option B aims at free organic rankings, option C attracts audiences with useful content, and option A pays partners commission on sales or leads they bring.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: The main difference between SEO and search engine marketing (SEM) through paid search ads is that:

options.a: SEO targets unpaid organic listings while paid search buys advertising positions
options.b: SEO is used only on television while paid search is used on radio
options.c: SEO is paid per click while paid search is completely free
options.d: SEO sends emails while paid search sends text messages

questions.explanation: SEO works to earn higher organic (free) rankings, while paid search places ads on the results page in return for payment, often per click. Option C reverses the two, and options B and D confuse search with broadcast, email and SMS.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: In search engine marketing, 'keywords' are:

options.a: The passwords that staff use to log into the company website
options.b: The short slogans painted on roadside billboards and buses
options.c: The names of the directors listed in a company's annual report
options.d: The words and phrases people type into a search engine to find something

questions.explanation: Keywords are the search terms people enter, and firms choose them carefully so that their website or ads appear for relevant searches. Options A, B and C have no role in how search engines match results to users.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A Port Harcourt hotel pays a search engine so that its advert appears at the top of the results when someone searches 'hotels in Port Harcourt', and it is charged only when a user clicks the advert. This is:

options.a: Search engine optimisation
options.b: Public relations
options.c: Pay-per-click search advertising
options.d: Email marketing

questions.explanation: Paying to appear on the results page and being charged per click is pay-per-click search advertising. Option A would involve improving the website to rank organically without paying per click, option D uses subscribers' inboxes, and option B seeks unpaid media coverage.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A Lagos skincare brand publishes free weekly videos and blog posts on how to care for skin in hot, humid weather, without pushing a direct sale in each one. Its main approach is:

options.a: Content marketing
options.b: Telemarketing
options.c: Affiliate marketing
options.d: Pay-per-click advertising

questions.explanation: Giving away helpful, relevant content to attract and build trust with an audience is content marketing. Option D involves paying for clicks on ads, option C pays partners for referred sales, and option B is selling by phone.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Email marketing is best described as:

options.a: Displaying adverts on roadside billboards and on the sides of buses
options.b: Sending commercial messages such as offers and newsletters to people on an email list
options.c: Improving a website's ranking in the free results shown by search engines
options.d: Paying influencers to recommend the firm's products on their social media pages

questions.explanation: Email marketing sends targeted messages, offers and newsletters directly to subscribers' inboxes. Option C is SEO, option D is influencer marketing, and option A is outdoor advertising.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Good email marketing practice is permission-based, which means the firm should:

options.a: Hide the option to unsubscribe from customers
options.b: Send messages only to people who have agreed (opted in) to receive them
options.c: Send as many emails as possible every day
options.d: Buy lists of strangers' email addresses and send to all of them

questions.explanation: Permission or opt-in email marketing contacts only people who have agreed to receive messages, which builds trust and avoids being treated as spam. Options A, C and D are poor practices that annoy recipients and damage the brand.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Unsolicited bulk commercial email sent to people who did not ask for it is commonly called:

options.a: Spam
options.b: Content marketing
options.c: An opt-in list
options.d: A newsletter

questions.explanation: Spam is unwanted bulk email sent without the receiver's permission, and it harms a brand's reputation. Option D is a regular email subscribers have signed up for, option C is a list of people who agreed to receive email, and option B is about providing valuable content.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: An online bookshop sends a monthly email with new arrivals and discount codes to customers who signed up on its website. This is:

options.a: Search engine optimisation
options.b: Affiliate marketing
options.c: Email marketing
options.d: Outdoor advertising

questions.explanation: Sending offers and updates to subscribers who signed up is email marketing. Option A is about search rankings, option D uses billboards and transit, and option B rewards partner sites for referred sales.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Affiliate marketing is best described as:

options.a: Placing the firm's adverts in daily newspapers and weekly magazines
options.b: Paying partners commission for each sale or lead they bring through referral links
options.c: Creating free educational content such as videos to attract an audience
options.d: Paying a search engine a fee for every click on the firm's advert

questions.explanation: In affiliate marketing, other people or websites promote the firm's products and earn a commission only when their link produces a sale or lead. Option D is pay-per-click, option C is content marketing, and option A is print advertising.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A Nigerian e-commerce site gives bloggers a unique link and pays them 5% commission only on purchases made by shoppers who click their link. This is:

options.a: Public relations
options.b: Influencer marketing paid as a flat fee
options.c: Affiliate marketing
options.d: Search engine optimisation

questions.explanation: Paying a commission only on sales that come through a partner's unique link is affiliate marketing. Option B pays for exposure regardless of sales, option D improves organic rankings, and option A seeks unpaid media coverage.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Influencer marketing is best described as:

options.a: Placing a firm's logo on hoardings around a football stadium
options.b: Improving the technical structure of a website so search engines rank it
options.c: Sending SMS alerts to every phone number held in a customer database
options.d: Partnering with individuals who have a large, engaged online following to promote a brand

questions.explanation: Influencer marketing uses people whom many others follow and trust online, such as content creators, to recommend a brand to their audience. Option B is SEO, option C is SMS marketing, and option A is sponsorship or outdoor advertising.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A drinks company pays a popular Nigerian comedy skit-maker with millions of Instagram followers to feature its product in his videos. This is:

options.a: Email marketing
options.b: Influencer marketing
options.c: Personal selling
options.d: Search engine optimisation

questions.explanation: Paying a person with a large, engaged following to feature a product is influencer marketing. Option A uses inboxes, option D improves search rankings, and option C is a salesperson dealing directly with a buyer.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: The key difference between affiliate marketing and influencer marketing, as usually defined, is that affiliate marketing:

options.a: Pays for exposure whether or not any sales result from it
options.b: Pays partners mainly according to the sales or leads they actually generate
options.c: Never uses the internet or any digital channel
options.d: Always involves famous celebrities with millions of followers

questions.explanation: Affiliate marketing is performance-based: partners are paid for the sales or leads their links bring. Influencer marketing focuses on the person's reach and influence, and is often paid for the promotion itself, as option A describes; options C and D are simply untrue.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Social media marketing is best described as:

options.a: Using social platforms to share content, engage users and build brand communities
options.b: Placing adverts on national radio stations during peak listening hours
options.c: Paying a commission to other websites only for the sales they refer
options.d: Sending printed letters and catalogues to customers' home addresses

questions.explanation: Social media marketing uses platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to post content, talk with users and build communities. Option D is direct mail, option C is affiliate marketing, and option B is broadcast advertising.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Mobile marketing is best described as:

options.a: Running adverts only on national television during prime time
options.b: Reaching consumers on their phones through SMS, apps, mobile sites and location-based offers
options.c: Advertising on buses and other vehicles that move around the city
options.d: Selling products from a moving van that travels between markets

questions.explanation: Mobile marketing targets people through their phones, using SMS, in-app ads, mobile websites and location-based offers. Options C and D involve physical movement, not mobile devices, and option A is broadcast advertising.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A Nigerian telecom operator sends subscribers text messages offering discounted data bundles that can be bought by dialling a short code. This is mainly an example of:

options.a: Mobile (SMS) marketing
options.b: Content marketing
options.c: Outdoor advertising
options.d: Search engine optimisation

questions.explanation: Sending promotional text messages to phone users is mobile marketing. Option B relies on publishing valuable content, option D is about search rankings, and option C uses billboards and other outdoor sites.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A marketing approach in which a message is designed so that people pass it on to others, spreading it rapidly like a virus, is called:

options.a: Telemarketing
options.b: Trade promotion
options.c: Viral marketing
options.d: Search engine optimisation

questions.explanation: Viral marketing creates messages people want to share, so the message spreads quickly from person to person. Option D is about search rankings, option B targets intermediaries, and option A uses phone calls.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Display advertising in digital marketing refers to:

options.a: Text messages sent to customers' phones
options.b: Products arranged on shelves in a supermarket
options.c: Unpaid news stories about a company
options.d: Visual adverts such as banners shown on websites and apps

questions.explanation: Display advertising places visual ads, such as banners and image or video ads, on websites and apps. Option A is SMS marketing, option B is in-store merchandising, and option C is publicity.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: In digital marketing, 'owned media' refers to:

options.a: Billboards and bus panels rented from outdoor advertising firms
options.b: Shares, reviews and mentions of the brand by customers and the press
options.c: Channels the firm controls itself, such as its website and official social media pages
options.d: Advertising space the firm buys on other people's websites and platforms

questions.explanation: Owned media are channels the brand controls, like its own website, app and social media accounts. Option D is paid media, option B is earned media, and option A is also paid space, just offline.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Customer reviews, social media shares and free press coverage that a brand receives because of what others say about it are called:

options.a: Earned media
options.b: Paid media
options.c: Owned media
options.d: Display media

questions.explanation: Earned media is exposure a brand gains through others, such as reviews, shares and news coverage, without paying for the space. Option B is bought advertising, option C is the brand's own channels, and option D refers to visual banner ads, which are paid.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Inbound digital marketing differs from outbound marketing in that inbound marketing:

options.a: Relies only on television and radio commercials
options.b: Avoids the internet entirely
options.c: Pushes messages at people through cold calls and interruptive adverts
options.d: Attracts customers to the firm through useful content, search and social media

questions.explanation: Inbound marketing pulls customers in by being found and offering value, for example through content, SEO and social media. Option C describes outbound marketing, and options A and B describe traditional offline methods.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Click-through rate (CTR) in digital advertising measures:

options.a: The proportion of people who saw an advert and then clicked on it
options.b: The time it takes to design an advert
options.c: The number of employees in the marketing department
options.d: The total amount of money spent on a campaign

questions.explanation: CTR compares the number of clicks an ad gets with the number of times it was shown, so it shows how attractive the ad is. Option D is campaign cost, and options B and C are internal measures unrelated to audience response.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: In digital marketing, a 'conversion' occurs when:

options.a: A visitor leaves the website without clicking or doing anything
options.b: A visitor completes a desired action, such as making a purchase or signing up
options.c: A firm changes its company logo and colours
options.d: An advert is shown on a roadside billboard

questions.explanation: A conversion is when a user does what the marketer wanted, such as buying, registering or downloading. Option A is a bounce, option C is a branding change, and option D is offline exposure.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: After a shopper looks at a pair of sneakers on a Nigerian online store but does not buy, adverts for the same sneakers follow her on other websites she visits. This technique is called:

options.a: Affiliate marketing
options.b: Search engine optimisation
options.c: Public relations
options.d: Retargeting (remarketing)

questions.explanation: Retargeting shows ads to people who have already visited a site or viewed a product, reminding them to come back and buy. Option B is about organic search, option A pays partners on referred sales, and option C seeks favourable unpaid coverage.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of digital marketing for small Nigerian businesses?

options.a: It works without any need for internet access
options.b: It guarantees that every customer will buy the product
options.c: It allows them to reach targeted audiences at relatively low cost
options.d: It removes all competition from the market

questions.explanation: Digital tools let small firms target the right people with modest budgets, helping them compete with bigger brands. Option B is untrue because no medium guarantees sales, option D is impossible, and option A is wrong because digital marketing depends on internet access.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of digital marketing?

options.a: Campaigns can reach audiences across the world
options.b: Results can be measured in real time
options.c: Messages can be personalised for different customers
options.d: Messages reach people who have no internet or mobile access

questions.explanation: Digital marketing depends on internet or mobile access, so it cannot reach people without it; that is a limitation, not an advantage. Options A, B and C are genuine advantages: measurability, personalisation and global reach.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following is a major challenge of digital marketing?

options.a: Inability to measure any campaign results
options.b: Concerns over customer data privacy and security
options.c: Being restricted to one small local area
options.d: Lack of any interaction with customers

questions.explanation: Collecting and using customer data raises privacy and security concerns, which firms must manage carefully. Options A, C and D are wrong because digital marketing is highly measurable, interactive and able to reach wide audiences.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: A restaurant in Abuja finds that a single angry customer's post about poor service is shared thousands of times within a day. This illustrates which challenge of digital marketing?

options.a: Online audiences never react to what brands do
options.b: Digital media reach only a handful of people
options.c: Digital messages cannot be shared with other users
options.d: Negative messages can spread very quickly and widely online

questions.explanation: Because online content is easy to share, a single negative post can spread fast and damage a brand, so firms must monitor and respond quickly. Options A, B and C contradict what happened in the scenario.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which statement best explains why digital marketers must keep learning and adjusting their strategies?

options.a: Digital platforms never change once they are created
options.b: Technology, platforms and search or social algorithms change rapidly
options.c: Offline media have completely disappeared
options.d: Consumers have stopped using the internet

questions.explanation: Digital channels change fast: new platforms appear and algorithms that decide who sees content are updated often, so strategies must keep adapting. Option A is false, and options C and D are untrue claims about consumers and offline media.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Why is it important for a firm's website to be mobile-friendly (responsive)?

options.a: Many users access the internet mainly through their phones
options.b: Search engines ignore all users on mobile phones
options.c: Mobile phones are unable to open any websites
options.d: People using mobile phones never make purchases

questions.explanation: A large share of internet users, especially in Nigeria, go online mainly on their phones, so a site that works well on mobile keeps them engaged. Options B, C and D are false statements about mobile devices and their users.

questions.topic: Online and Offline Media and Digital Marketing
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between online and offline media in a modern marketing communication plan?

options.a: Online media have fully replaced offline media in every market
options.b: They must always carry completely different messages
options.c: They can be combined so that each supports the other in an integrated campaign
options.d: Offline media should never be used once a firm has a website

questions.explanation: Most firms use both: offline media for broad reach and credibility, online media for targeting, interaction and measurement, with a consistent message across them. Options A and D wrongly write off offline media, and option B goes against the idea of a unified, integrated message.
